# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

> Cutting a release? Follow [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md) — bump
> `package.json`, roll `## [Unreleased]` to a dated `## [X.Y.Z]`, then tag `vX.Y.Z`
> (all three must match).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **The Nether works in online worlds (protocol v3→v4; save format v18 and worldgen 11 unchanged)**: light a portal in a co-op world and step through, exactly like single-player — and the party can split, with some players in the overworld and some in the Nether at once. The player list tags anyone who's "· Nether", a toast announces each crossing, and travel is seamless on the same connection (no reconnect). Server side, a room now runs an authoritative engine **per active dimension** ("dimension shards"): the overworld always, the nether born lazily on the first travel (or a rejoin whose save slice says nether) and persisted + dropped after `NETHER_SHARD_LINGER_MS` (60 s, env-tunable) once empty — and because the per-voxel light cache turns out to be renderer-only, **headless server engines now skip the light bake entirely (~40 MB and a full-world BFS saved per engine)**, so a two-shard room costs about what a one-engine room did before and the 512 MB Fly VM sizing is unchanged. Everything dimension-scoped got a real seam: tick channels and mob keyframes fan out per dimension (a cross-dimension keyframe would mass-prune a replica's mobs), the melee lag-comp history ring is per-shard, every pose/cmd carries a required dimension stamp (the travel race guard — frames in flight across a swap are dropped, never force-pose-fought), persistence composes both world halves at the room level, the day clock mirrors from the overworld (sleep counts only overworld players), and the owner's Peaceful despawns hostiles in every shard. The client rebuilds its replica engine and renderer in place around the live socket when the server says `dim`, prunes/adopts other players' avatars as they cross (`playerDim`), and a reconnect that raced a travel adopts the new dimension before resyncing. Deliberate scope: mobs (pets included) and vehicles stay behind — they are dimension state (your wolf waits by the portal); a mounted player can't accrue portal dwell at all (a raft drifting through a frame must never travel — this also fixes single-player); in-Nether deaths still respawn in the Nether. A new two-browser e2e drives the whole journey — a host builds and ignites a frame with real networked block placements, travels, is followed, and comes home — and [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) now carries the version-bump rollout runbook this deploy will follow.

### Fixed

- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.
- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).
- **A bed respawn point is now honored only in its own dimension**: the spawn point stored bare block coordinates, and the same coordinates index a different voxel in each world — so dying in the Nether could false-positive on whatever happened to occupy the overworld bed's cell there. Bed spawn points now carry a dimension stamp (optional save field, additive — old saves read as overworld); respawn falls through to a safe local spot when the bed belongs to the other world.
- **Deflaked the simulated-latency FIFO (a real reorder, not a test artifact)**: the latency-simulation knob scheduled one `setTimeout` per delayed message, relying on the timer heap to fire equal-deadline timers in creation order — but that tie-breaking is not stable in Bun, and the monotonic delivery cursor _clamps_ every message behind a high jitter draw to the exact same deadline, making ties the common case. Result: rare genuine reordering of simulated-latency traffic (caught by the jitter-FIFO unit test going red on `main`, ~2/100 locally). Each direction now drains through a queued **delay line** — the same cursor, but one timer chain delivering in queue order, so FIFO comes from the queue rather than from timer tie-breaking; `dispose()` clears both lines, so no stray delivery timers outlive a session. Dev/testing code path only (simulated latency is never on in real play) — no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change — though the lagged multiplayer e2e steps (400±100 ms) inherit the stronger ordering guarantee.
- **CI: forks no longer attempt (and fail) prod deploys**: the `deploy-web` / `deploy-server` jobs now carry a `github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'` guard. The upstream repo syncs this workflow but holds none of the deploy secrets, so every push to its `main` went red on `curl -X POST ""` / an unauthenticated `flyctl deploy` — nothing ever deployed (secrets are repo-scoped), it was pure noise. Outside this repo the jobs now skip instead of fail.
- **Deflaked the worldgen-determinism e2e**: the spec paused the engine from its test body, but the game had already been simulating live through the whole boot window (menus → first rendered frames) — and a fresh seed-1337 world is _not_ free of random-tickable blocks (worldgen leaves ~31 cave-exposed dirt columns beside grass and ~23 growable kelp stalks within random-tick range of spawn), so on a slow CI runner a `Math.random` grass-spread or kelp-growth roll could land one block edit before the hash and trip the `changes.length === 0` guard (the digest itself was never wrong — the guard fired exactly as designed). The `gamePage` fixture gains a `pauseOnBoot` option that traps the `window.__monecraft` assignment and pauses synchronously **before the engine's first step**, so the hashed bytes are provably untouched by simulation; the determinism spec opts in. Test-only — no product code, save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-07-08

### Added

- **Version badge on the menu**: a muted `v0.15.0 · <sha>` badge sits in the bottom-right corner of every menu screen (the welcome gate, account home, world select), so any deployed build is identifiable at a glance; with a commit SHA present it links to that commit on GitHub. The version comes from `package.json` and the short SHA from Vercel's `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`, both injected into the client bundle at build time via `next.config.mjs` (locally, with no SHA, it reads `… · dev`). Along the way this corrected a release-hygiene bug: `package.json`'s `version` had been left at `0.14.0` when `0.15.0` was cut (the release commit only edited the changelog) — it's now `0.15.0`, matching the tag, and [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md) documents the release steps so the three stay in lockstep.
- **The Nether — a second dimension behind an obsidian portal (save v17→v18; worldgen 11 and protocol v3 unchanged)**: build a standing obsidian rectangle (2×3 up to 4×4 interior, corners required), strike an inner face with **flint & steel** (1 sliver ore + 1 coal), and step through into a sealed ember world — netherrack caverns under a bedrock sky, hanging **glowstone**, **lava seas**, and perpetual hostiles: the **imp** (a fast melee brute) and the **scorcher** (a hovering fire-spirit lobbing dodgeable-but-heavy fireballs). Down deep lies **blazite ore** (diamond-pickaxe-gated): smelt it into ingots and forge the **post-diamond gear tier** — pickaxe (chews obsidian), sword (under only the Dragon Sword), and spear. Glowstone shatters into dust; 4 dust recombine into a placeable torch-strength light. Portals come out at the same coordinates in the other world, reusing a nearby portal or building a fresh one on a safe pad; travel re-validates the frame (a de-framed surface clears instead of carrying you), breaking frame obsidian extinguishes the surface immediately, beds refuse (no morning to skip to), and **dying in the Nether respawns you in the Nether**. Four advancements mark the milestones. Engineering shape: **swap-on-travel** — one live dimension per engine; travel writes an ordinary save (the player flipped into the target dimension plus a one-shot arrival anchor) and remounts, so no dual-world state exists anywhere. The save's top-level world fields remain the overworld's and the nether rides an additive `dimensions` section that any engine re-emits verbatim (the server round-trips nether builds without knowing they exist — protocol untouched; **portals are single-player only for now**, refused with a toast in online worlds). The nether generator is its own deterministic byte contract (portable noise, own PRNG streams, its own SHA-256 baselines) so overworld bytes are untouched and `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 11 — and the long-documented worldgen staleness guard is now actually **enforced** at boot (`worldgenVersion` stamps the save; a mismatch discards the world half and reboots from seed, with unstamped pre-v18 saves grandfathered). The renderer gains per-dimension environment profiles (ember sky, close fog, no celestials; a raised shader light floor is the skyless dimension's ambient glow), and the minimap learned to see through the bedrock roof.
- **Buckets, movable fluids & obsidian — the nether epic's opening act**: craft a **bucket** (3 sliver ore; empties stack to 16, a filled bucket rides alone) and right-click to **scoop** the aimed water or lava block and **pour** it back out against a solid face — the game's first fluid pickup/placement (lava was worldgen-only and untouchable). Fluids are **still**: no flow simulation, so a scooped ocean cell leaves a neat one-block hole and a poured block stays put; a poured lava block glows (max light) and burns exactly like the native floods, and a pour that would entomb you rolls back like ordinary placement. Pour **water directly onto lava** and it hisses into **obsidian** (BlockId 90, appended) — the game's only obsidian source and its hardest mineable block: **diamond-pickaxe-gated**, hardness 40, deliberately a grind because it is the portal-frame material of the dimension work that follows. Under the hood: a new `ItemDef.stackSize` caps per-item stacks, the water scoop reuses the fishing-bobber `waterSurfaceRaycast` (the solid raycast passes through water), and every mutation rides the ordinary `blockChanges.set` chokepoint — **no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change** (v17 / worldgen 11 / protocol v3 untouched).
- **Slabs & stairs — half-blocks for real architecture**: craft **slabs** (3 planks/stone/cobble → 6, filling the bottom half of a cell) and **stairs** (6 → 4, a slab plus a raised back that faces away from you when placed — turned by your look direction, so you walk straight up what you just laid; every facing drops the one item). They are the game's first **partial solids**: one set of shape boxes drives both the mesh and a new partial-height collision, so you stand exactly where the block looks like it holds you. Half-blocks count as ground for mobs (a slab floor reads at its real half height) but are **not** valid support for floor-mounted fittings — doors, redstone components, and rails all refuse them. BlockIds 75–89 appended, craft-only: **no save-format or worldgen change**.
- **Auto step-up — half-height rises no longer need a jump**: grounded walking now climbs rises up to `STEP_UP_HEIGHT` (0.55) automatically — up a slab, up each half of a stair, along any half-high terrain lip — while **full blocks still require the jump** (Minecraft parity; the dial is in `config.ts`). This is a deliberate global movement-feel change, not just a slabs feature: it applies anywhere a half-height edge occurs. Airborne and flying movement never auto-steps, the crouch edge-guard is unchanged, and online play needs no protocol or server-clamp change (the pose clamp's existing vertical slack covers the per-tick rise).
- **The drowned — night oceans bite back**: the water gets its first hostile. At night (difficulty-gated like every hostile; none on Peaceful), sunken teal zombies rise in open water near you — never point-blank under a swimmer — and pursue you through the water in full 3D, striking with the same line-of-sight, difficulty scaling, and knockback rules as a land mob's melee. They are **strictly water-bound**: the same movement gate that keeps fish in the water keeps a drowned from ever walking ashore (knocked onto land, it suffocates like a beached cod), and being submerged shields it from the daylight burn — so a guarded wreck stays guarded until you deal with its keeper. Drops: rotten flesh, a 50% kelp, and a **7% sliver spear** (the trident nod); the first kill unlocks **Revenge of the Tides**. Population is bounded by its own `DROWNED_CAP` inside the shared hostile cap, and the fish top-up now counts only passives so a full night of drowned can't starve the cod schools. No new blocks, no save/worldgen/protocol change — the drowned is a fungible hostile riding the existing mob machinery (recipe-book hints also learned that chance-gated drops aren't an item's "natural source", so the spear keeps its Craft hint).
- **Rails & minecarts — lay track and ride it**: craft **rails** (3 sliver ore + 3 wood → 16) as flat floor overlays like wire (solid support required, pop off when it breaks), and a **minecart** (5 sliver ore) that places onto an aimed rail and is ridden with the same board/dismount controls as boats — but rail-guided: forward throttles, back brakes then reverses, and the track does the steering, turning corners wherever two lines meet at a right angle (no curve piece; orientation is derived from neighboring rails, never stored). Two special rails hook into redstone-lite: the **powered rail** (2 gold + 1 dust + 2 wood → 4) is a consumer that boosts carts past cruise speed while lit and **stops them dead while unpowered** (a lever beside one is a station switch — and a parked cart on a lit one launches the way it faces, so button-powered launcher tracks work riderless), and the **detector rail** (1 sliver + 1 dust + 1 cobble → 2) is a source that powers its neighbors like a pressed plate while a cart sits on it (parked carts also hold real pressure plates down — trap wiring welcome). Riderless carts coast and friction parks them; mining the rail out from under a cart strands it. First ride unlocks the **On Rails** advancement. Under the hood the cart is a third `VehicleKind` riding the existing vehicle persistence and multiplayer replication unchanged (**no save/worldgen/protocol bump** — BlockIds 70–74 appended, the powered/detector parity pairs joining the redstone family), the wheel-on-rail clack is a distance-paced ZZFX tick, and mounting any vehicle now correctly silences footsteps (riding a ship used to "walk" audibly).
- **Redstone-lite — buildable power circuits**: craft **Redstone Dust** (1 gold ore + 1 coal → 8; redstone _ore_ worldgen is deferred to a future worldgen batch so existing worlds keep their builds) and wire up **levers**, **stone buttons** (~1 s pulse), **pressure plates** (players _and_ mobs trigger them — traps work), and **redstone torches**. Dust places as flat **wire** that carries a signal up to 15 blocks (climbing single-block steps); powered circuits force **doors** open/closed on power edges (hand-toggling still works in between), ignite **TNT**, and light the new **redstone lamp** (4 dust + 2 glass, a switchable full-brightness light). The torch is an **inverter** — it turns off while its support block is powered and never powers its own support — so NOT gates and blinking two-torch clocks are buildable; circuits update on a fixed 0.1 s tick (`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS` in `config.ts`, with `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE` and `REDSTONE_BUTTON_PRESS_SECONDS` alongside). Under the hood every power state is a BlockId variant riding the ordinary block diff — **no save-format or worldgen change** (v17 / worldgen 11 untouched), zero new assets — and the simulation runs server-side in online worlds with its edits replicating through the existing tick journal, so multiplayer needed no wire code. Components mount on solid blocks and pop off (dropping their item) when the support breaks; a new "Circuit Breaker" advancement lands on your first lever flip.

### Changed

- **Production deploys are gated on a green CI run**: Vercel (web) and Fly.io (game server) previously auto-deployed on every push to `main` in parallel with CI, so a red build could still ship. Both platform on-push auto-deploys are now off — Vercel via a new `vercel.json` (`git.deploymentEnabled: { "main": false }`), Fly in its dashboard — and two new `deploy-web` / `deploy-server` jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (both `needs: [verify, e2e]`, push-to-main only) are the sole trigger. So a merge only reaches prod after lint/typecheck/test/build **and** the browser e2e all pass; a failing (or flaky) CI blocks the deploy until re-run. `deploy-web` fires a Vercel Deploy Hook (the build stays Git-connected, so the version badge's commit SHA is still injected); `deploy-server` runs `flyctl deploy` with the pinned `server/fly.toml` config. Needs two repo secrets (`VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`, `FLY_API_TOKEN`); `vercel --prod` / `bun run deploy:server` remain as manual escape hatches. See docs/deploy.md → Continuous deployment.
- **Production domain moves to `mc.ainaive.com`**: the app is served from `mc.ainaive.com` instead of `monecraft.vercel.app`; the old domain 308-redirects to it (path-preserving), so invite links already shared under `monecraft.vercel.app/join/<token>` keep working. No code change — the app derives its origin from the browser at runtime (invite links, auth client, service-worker cache scope all follow the serving domain), and the Fly game server does no Origin/CORS check, so nothing on the server side is touched. The one coupled value is the `BETTER_AUTH_URL` Vercel env var (now `https://mc.ainaive.com`, or sign-in hangs); `NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL` still points at the Fly server, unchanged. See docs/deploy.md → Custom domain.
- **World saves move from localStorage to IndexedDB — big builds no longer risk the quota cliff**: a heavily-edited world's save is unbounded JSON, and localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin cap was the likeliest real data loss now that the PWA multiplies long-lived offline worlds ("Save failed" forever once over the line). Saves now live in an IndexedDB store (database `monecraft`) with far larger quotas; existing worlds migrate transparently on first launch (copy-then-delete per world — a mid-migration failure can never lose a blob), and the small profile/world manifests stay in localStorage. The unload save rides `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange`/`pagehide` with an explicitly committed transaction — mobile app-switch now flushes immediately (beforeunload never fired reliably there) instead of waiting for the next 15s autosave. The pause-menu "Saved" toast now means the write durably committed. Browsers without IndexedDB (some private modes) fall back to the old localStorage behavior wholesale; returning players also get a `navigator.storage.persist()` request for eviction protection. Save format itself is unchanged (still v17) — only the container moved; cloud saves and online worlds are untouched.

### Fixed

- **Unreadable menu section headings**: the "Online Worlds" and "Singleplayer" headings on the profile → Worlds screen rendered in the browser-default **black** on the dark menu background — `.menu-online-title` set a size and opacity but never a text color, so the `<h3>`s inherited black instead of the menu's near-white. They now use the same `--mc-text-light` + text-shadow as every other menu label.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-07-06

### Added

- **Touch play — the installed PWA is now playable on tablets and landscape phones**: touch devices get on-screen controls automatically (an Auto/On/Off override lives in Pause → Options, and flipping it hot-swaps the input method mid-world). Move on a left virtual joystick — re-engage it quickly and push forward to sprint; drag anywhere on the world to look, **tap** to attack, **press and hold** to mine (a camera swipe never digs — gesture discrimination has a hard slop boundary); buttons cover Jump (double-tap toggles Creative flight, relabeled Rise/Descend while flying), Sneak (a toggle), Place/interact/throw, and a contextual Eat that appears while holding food. Tap hotbar slots to select; **long-press** any slot or recipe entry for the details desktop shows on hover (durability, missing ingredients — the recipe book's whole help system). The pause menu gains an **Emergency Unstuck** button (Shift+U's home for keyboardless players — and a discoverability win on desktop). Under the hood, touch is a second implementation of the same input-controller contract the keyboard uses — the engine is input-agnostic and untouched; desktop play is byte-identical, and the layout gains safe-area (notch) padding, dynamic-viewport heights, and short-landscape breakpoints that desktop never triggers. Feel constants (look sensitivity, tap/hold windows) live in `config.ts` for one-line on-device tuning — a real-device pass is the named follow-up (see docs/testing.md's checklist). Deferred for now: touch chat typing, the debug overlay, and tap-a-block targeting (aiming is center-crosshair, as in Minecraft PE classic).
- **Melee lag compensation — clicking the mob you SEE now hits it at any ping (protocol v2→v3)**: in an online world your screen renders mobs 125–450 ms in the past (the interpolation delay), so at high ping a melee swing aimed dead at a mob used to whiff — the server judged it against positions your screen hadn't shown yet. Attacks now carry the instant of the world you were looking at (the frame's render time on the server clock), and the server rewinds **target selection** to that instant against its own recorded mob history, bounded to 900 ms (`MELEE_REWIND_MAX_MS`) — damage, knockback, and kill credit still land on the live mob, so nothing resurrects and no consequence time-travels. Anything degenerate (an unsynced clock, a stale or future stamp, a mob spawned since the viewed tick) simply judges live, exactly as before; single-player is untouched. A 12-attacks/second server budget keeps the rewind window from being trawled by scripted spam. The protocol bump means the web app and game server deploy together; a stale tab is refused cleanly at the door. Bow arrows keep current behavior on purpose — travel time means players already lead their shots; rewinding swept projectile paths is heavier machinery for less felt benefit (future work).
- **Offline play (PWA, part 2)**: after one online visit, single-player boots with no connection — a hand-rolled service worker (`public/sw.js`, no workbox/serwist dependency) precaches the app shell and its static chunks, serves navigations network-first (deploys land normally and apply silently on the next online load), and **never touches** `/api/*`, the game-server connection, or invite links, so accounts, cloud saves, and multiplayer behave exactly as before. In development the registration component instead unregisters workers and clears caches, keeping `bun run dev` immune to a stale prod worker on the same origin. Pinned by classifier unit tests (`tests/sw.test.ts`) and an offline e2e (`e2e/pwa.e2e.ts`) that cuts the network and boots a world from the worker's cache.
- **Welcome-gate offline hint**: opened without a connection (say, as an installed PWA on a plane), the welcome gate says "Offline — local play only." so the working door is obvious. Sign in stays enabled — its own failure copy already covers a dead network — and the hint tracks connectivity live via a new `useOnlineStatus` hook.
- **Installable app identity (PWA, part 1)**: the app now ships a web-app manifest (name **Monecraft**, standalone landscape window, theme colors matched to the menu gate) and browser/install icons — an 8×8 grass-block face generated at request time from the same `BLOCK_COLORS` palette as the world atlas, via `ImageResponse` pixel code (`lib/ui/appIcon.tsx`), keeping the zero-binary-assets rule. The document title changes from "Minecraft Clone" to **Monecraft**, matching the in-game logo. Offline support (the service worker) lands separately.
- **Zero-config local dev**: `bun run dev` with no `DATABASE_URL` now falls back to an ephemeral in-memory PGlite database (with a one-time console notice) instead of 500-ing on the first online request — the full accounts/cloud-saves stack works out of the box in dev, resetting on restart. Production still requires a real `DATABASE_URL`.
- **Optimistic block placement — building feels instant at any ping**: in an online world, placing a block now happens on your screen at click time instead of a full round-trip later (previously ~1.5 s of nothing at a 700 ms ping). The replica predicts only when it's certain the click is a pure block placement (right block in hand, nothing interactive or ridable in the aim) — every other right-click keeps its server-decided behavior; the command always travels and the server stays fully authoritative. Its block journal confirms the prediction, overrides it (you lost a race — the other player's block appears and your item comes back), or, if no answer arrives in time, the block quietly reverts with the item refunded. Your own placement sound/particles play once, at click time — the server echo is recognized (via the new event attribution) and swallowed.
- **Predictive block breaking + instant swing feedback**: mining in an online world now breaks the block on your screen the moment the crack completes, instead of showing a fully-cracked block that lingers for a round-trip (chests still wait for the server — their contents are server-owned). Drops, XP, and tool wear stay server-authoritative and arrive on the private delta a moment later; a break the server disagrees with reverts just like a rejected placement. Attacking plays your swing animation and sound at click time (the echo is recognized and swallowed) — hit results still come from the server, so combat at high ping remains delayed; that's the next frontier (server-side lag compensation), not this change.
- **Net debug tooling — jittered latency simulation + F3 connection stats**: `window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms, jitterMs)` now takes an optional per-message jitter (delivery stays FIFO, like real TCP), seedable via `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_JITTER_MS`, and the F3 overlay gains two lines while online — RTT/jitter/interpolation delay and in/out KB/s — so high-latency play can be reproduced and observed locally instead of across an ocean.

### Changed

- **Tick events are attributed to the acting player**: a server room now stamps `playerId` onto every gameplay event that has an actor (block edits, swings, and so on — advancement/join/leave events already carried one). Wire-compatible (the tick's `ev` envelope always allowed the field); groundwork for the client telling its own action echoes apart from other players'.
- **Smooth remote players/mobs on jittery connections — adaptive interpolation + hardened clock sync**: the interpolation delay (how far in the past remote entities render) is no longer a fixed 125 ms — it now sizes itself from measured tick-arrival jitter (125–450 ms, drifting at most 60 ms/s so nothing visibly warps). On a clean LAN nothing changes; on a jittery long-haul link remote players stop freeze-and-snapping. The server-clock estimate switches from a pure EWMA to an NTP-style min-RTT pick (the pong least inflated by queueing anchors the offset; slewed, snapping only on reconnect-sized jumps), and pings tighten from 2 s to 1 s to keep that window fresh.
- **Multiplayer wire diet — quantized poses + compression**: replicated positions now round to 2 decimals and angles/velocities to 3 before hitting the wire (raw doubles serialized at up to 17 characters each), and the game server offers **permessage-deflate**, which browsers negotiate automatically — together cutting per-tick payloads several-fold on the same JSON envelope (no protocol bump; old and new clients interoperate). Groundwork for playing across continents, where every queued byte on a congested route adds delay.
- **Game server rightsized to its real usage**: the Fly VM drops from 2 GB to **512 MB** (still `shared-cpu-2x`), and with it `MAX_ROOMS` from 6 to **3** — rooms are ~74 MB each, so the two must scale together or a full house would OOM the machine. Live metrics showed the 2 GB ceiling was never approached; raising capacity later is `fly scale memory` plus the env. Applies on the next `bun run deploy:server`.
- **CI: browser e2e runs on merges to `main`, not every PR push**: the Playwright suite takes several times longer than the verify job and was the long pole on PR iteration. PRs keep the full verify gate (lint, typecheck, format, tests, build); e2e still gates what actually lands on `main`, and renderer/input/shell changes run it locally before landing per AGENTS.md.
- **The menu now opens on a welcome gate**: logged out, the first screen is an explicit choice — **Sign in** (online worlds, synced profiles, cloud saves; opens a dedicated sign-in screen whose "I need an account" toggle registers) or **Play locally** (browser profiles and worlds, no account) — replacing the local-profile screen with an account panel embedded under it, which read as "create a local profile to play" and misled new users about where accounts fit. Sign-in/register is a standalone screen with no local-profile UI beside it; the local menus gain a Back to the gate; signing out lands on the gate. A signed-in reload skips the gate entirely (no flash) straight to the account home, and resuming a world mid-tab is untouched. On the account home, the prominent **Play locally** button becomes a quiet **"Local worlds on this browser"** footer link — signed-in play lives in the online profiles, while local worlds (and their cloud-save Upload/Download) stay one click away.

### Fixed

- **Online co-op — players in the same world couldn't see each other on prod** (each showed "Players (1)"): the deploy runbook now pins the Fly game server to a **single machine** (`fly scale count 1`) and documents the invariant. `fly launch` had provisioned the default two-machine HA pair; rooms live in one process's memory with no cross-instance coordination, so each machine hosted its own independent copy of the same world and the edge load-balancer split the players between them. Docs-only — no code change; the ops fix is one command on the live app.
- **Invite page — Create account is now a visible button**: the logged-out account panel on the `/join/<token>` landing page shows **Create account** next to **Sign in** instead of hiding registration behind Sign in → "I need an account". (In the main menu this fix is superseded by the welcome gate above, which routes sign-in/register through the dedicated screen.)

## [0.13.0] - 2026-07-04

### Added

The replica engine outlives its socket — a non-fatal drop (idle timeout, redeploy, network blip) walks a back-off ladder (1/2/4/8/8 s), mints a **fresh** join ticket each rung, and re-handshakes to re-sync the same world in place (an amber "Reconnecting…" badge, not a dead-end modal); fatal closes (bad ticket, kick, slow-client) don't retry. A `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` knob on `window.__monecraft.net` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`) injects artificial delay for local testing. World owners can **revoke every outstanding invite link** in one click from the menu. The game server gains admin ops behind `ADMIN_TOKEN`: a per-room replay log (`GET /rooms/:id/log`) that `scripts/replay.ts` reconstructs offline, an owner **kick** (`POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`), and `/rooms` bandwidth (`kbOutPerSec`) alongside the tick gauges — plus `scripts/loadSim.ts`, a synthetic N-client soak that reports server tick p95 vs the 50 ms budget for tuning `MAX_ROOMS`. Net constants are documented in tuning.md and an ops runbook in online.md.
- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link — the offline single-player game is entirely unchanged and still needs no account or connection. The menu grows an **Online Worlds** section (create a server-backed world, copy an invite link) and an **Account** panel (one-click guest, or upgrade to keep your worlds); opening an invite link (`/join/<token>`) signs the visitor in — as a guest if they're new — accepts the membership, and drops the world into their list. In-world you see the other players (named avatars overhead), share every block edit / mob / chest / day-night with them, and **chat** with `T`/`Enter`; a ping badge and disconnect notice track the connection. The client mounts the **same** renderer/audio/HUD/input stack on a _replica_ engine (`NetworkSession`, `lib/net/`): it worldgens byte-identically from the server's seed, applies the gzipped world sync, predicts only its own movement (streamed at tick rate; the server clamps speed/teleports and owns hunger/health/inventory via change-only self-deltas), renders remote players and mobs ~125 ms in the past from interpolation buffers, and reroutes gameplay commands up the wire through the engine's `routeDispatch` hook — so the input controller and every UI panel behave exactly as in single-player. Pause is personal (the world keeps running; "Save & Quit" becomes "Leave world"), the night skips only when everyone's in bed, and mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT). A full-stack Playwright spec (`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`) drives two browsers through invite → join → shared edit → chat against the real Next app (on an in-process `pglite://memory` Postgres) and Bun game server, no external services. **v1 scope cuts**: rafts/ships aren't boardable online, in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only their hits), and advancements/stats accrue to the room's primary player only.
- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket — protocol v1 (JSON envelopes + one gzipped world-sync frame; total validation of hostile input with a per-command allow-list), 20 Hz fixed-tick rooms with client-pose clamping (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport rejection → forcePose) that keeps hunger/stats/fall-damage server-authoritative, change-only per-player self-deltas, deadbanded 10 Hz mob replication with 5 s keyframes, chat with rate limits, backpressure shedding + slow-client kicks, join-restore/leave-persist through the v17 save, 60 s dirty persistence + SIGTERM drain, idle room eviction, /health + token-guarded /rooms diagnostics, PERSISTENCE=memory for DB-less runs, a netProbe CLI client, and Dockerfile + fly.toml. The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).
- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.

### Changed

- **Multi-player engine core** (save **v16→v17**; single-player behavior unchanged — the full e2e suite passes as before): the engine now models N players in one world, with single-player as the one-entry case of the same state. `GameState.players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>` absorbs every per-player field (inventory, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player timers); the old flat fields remain as accessor aliases onto the primary player for the shell/tests/console, with an ESLint guard banning them inside engine systems. All 23 systems take the acting player explicitly: mobs hunt the nearest targetable player (Creative/Spectator excluded) and anchor flee/pet-follow on the nearest of any mode; arrows/explosions hit any/all players in range; spawn directors center waves on a random party member and scale the hostile cap by `ceil(players/2)`; dungeon spawners arm for any player in radius; random ticks split their budget across players; raid rewards pay every living player. The night skips only when **every** eligible player is in bed (new `wakeUp` command backs out pre-fade). `dispatch`/`applyLook` take the commanding player's id; `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (join restores the persisted v17 slice, leave serializes it back), `setPlayerInput`, and the `authority`/`headless` engine options are the surface a multiplayer server drives. Saves migrate automatically (v16 flat fields wrap into `players: [{id:"local",…}]`; pet owners become real player ids).
- **Input intents** (no behavior change): the engine's `FrameInput` no longer carries DOM key codes, CapsLock, or pointer-lock state — the input controller reduces them to abstract movement intents (`forward/back/left/right/jump/sprint/crouch` + `mineHeld`). Key bindings and cursor capture now live entirely in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`; the engine simulates the same regardless of input source, which is what a multiplayer client's per-tick intent packets (and a future keybinding screen) require.
- **Tick driver extraction** (no behavior change): the rAF loop's catch-up substepping moved from `useMinecraftGame` into `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts` (`createAccumulator`), alongside a new drift-corrected `createFixedTicker` — the 20 Hz driver a headless multiplayer server will step worlds with. Unit-tested with a fake clock (catch-up, debt-drop cap, no drift under chronically-late callbacks).
- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat. Terrain is visually unchanged (same formulas; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched), but exact bytes shift: **existing worlds reboot from their seed and discard block edits**, per the standard worldgen-bump policy. Digests re-baselined into the new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`; a new Playwright spec (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`) proves Chromium/V8 regenerates the exact Bun/JSC baseline.

  - **Shipwrecks**: flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage — and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and **all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged** (no re-roll exploit, no save bump)
  - **Buried treasure & the treasure map**: hold a map (wreck loot, or a rare fishing catch) and a **compass pill** points at the _nearest_ unearthed hoard while red **X**s mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a **seed-pure beach proxy** (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires the new **treasureUnearthed** event → **X Marks the Spot** advancement + a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic
- **Rafts and ships**: craftable water vehicles on **zero binary assets**. Hold a **raft** (4 planks + 2 wood) or **ship** (8 planks + 3 wood + 2 string), right-click a water surface to place it, then travel without swimming. Rafts are smaller and slower and require right-click to board; ships are larger/faster and auto-board when you step onto the deck. Movement uses the existing WASD controls while mounted, and crouch dismounts to a nearby safe spot. Placed vehicles persist across reloads, so the save schema bumps **v15 → v16** with an additive `vehicles` field; vehicle items are string ids and vehicles are entities, not blocks, so **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). Rafts and ships live in their own **Vehicles** crafting category; placing plays a wooden thunk and a failed placement (no open water, blocked, or at the **`MAX_VEHICLES`** (64) per-world cap) plays a "can't place here" denial cue. A saved boat is never dropped on reload even if the water beneath it was later removed, and boat travel no longer inflates the walked-distance statistic.
- **Generated villages, villager professions & raids** (Living World, PR 2 of 2): the world is now inhabited and contested.
  - **Villages**: clusters of houses generate on flat, dry land — terraced and built so they're actually visible (the old loose houses rarely fit natural terrain, so they barely appeared). Villager **residents** spawn and live there and **persist with the world**; villagers no longer scatter loosely (a village-less seed falls back to a few wandering ones near spawn, so trading is always available). Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** — existing worlds of the old version reboot from their seed, and the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined — with no save-schema change for the villages themselves (residents ride the v14 `mobs` field). Villages run on their own decoupled PRNG (`villageRand`) placed last, so every other generation pass stays byte-identical to a village-less world of the same seed.
  - **Villager professions**: each villager is a **farmer, blacksmith, librarian, or cleric** and offers only its own slice of the trade economy (a sell + a buy each), its smock tinted to its profession. Opening a villager filters the Trading recipe book to its offers and gates the craft command — you can't craft a blacksmith trade while talking to a farmer (a spoof guard on dispatch, not just the UI). Save schema bumps **v14→v15** (a resident's additive `profession` on its `SavedMob`; pre-v15 villagers load professionless and the engine assigns one).
  - **Raids**: a craftable **Ominous Horn** (3 gold ore + 2 bone + 4 gunpowder) sounded near a village calls down **`RAID_WAVE_COUNT` (3)** waves of a new **raider** mob; clear them all for an emerald + XP reward, or — if every nearby villager dies first — the village falls. Raiders hunt villagers (and your pets defend), reusing the mob allegiance and mob-vs-mob combat from PR 1, so they needed no AI change. A raid is transient (`state.raid`, like the boss — a reload cancels it), so there's no save bump beyond the additive horn item; worldgen is unchanged (stays 9).
- **Tameable companions & a living mob world** (Living World, PR 1 of 2): wolves and cats now roam the world, and feeding a wild one its treat — a **bone** for a wolf, **raw fish** for a cat — tames it (a ~1-in-3 `TAME_CHANCE`; the treat is eaten either way). A tamed pet becomes a loyal **ally** that follows you, **sits/stays** on a right-click (holding a non-treat), and **fights hostiles for you** — its kills drop loot and XP straight to you. It recalls (teleports) to you past `PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE`, and **survives save/reload** — the first mob the game ever persists. Bred pets pass on their ownership, so puppies and kittens are owned allies too. Zero new assets (procedural wolf/cat models + ZZFX barks/meows); the save schema bumps **v13 → v14** (additive persisted pets), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - This lands two reusable foundations. **Mob allegiance**: every mob carries a `faction` (wild/hostile/ally/villager/raider) that drives a shared enmity table, so mobs fight _each other_ — hostiles now hunt and attack **villagers** (who flee), and your pets defend you. A fighter re-scans for the nearest enemy only every `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS`, so the per-frame mob tick stays O(N); mob-vs-mob combat is melee-only and uses raw damage (difficulty scales player-facing hits only). A kill credits loot/XP by the **victim's** faction — a pet's kill feeds you, a slain villager or pet yields nothing. **Mob persistence**: a minimal `SavedMob` (only tamed pets in this release) round-trips through `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs`, re-grounding each pet onto the current surface on load; the fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot as before
- **Advancements & statistics**: the game gains a progression meta — running **statistics** (blocks mined, monsters slain, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, animals bred, distance travelled, time played, deaths, jumps, villager trades) and a tight, flat set of **16 advancements**, one per major system (mine a log/stone/sliver/diamond, craft a pickaxe, craft a furnace, fire a bow, slay a hostile, defeat the Dragon Lord, breed animals, harvest wheat, catch a fish, enchant an item, drink a potion, sleep, trade with a villager). All on **zero new assets** — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — and the save schema bumps **v12 → v13** (additive), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - Press **L** to open a dedicated two-tab overlay (mutually exclusive with the inventory; the pause menu won't open over it): an **Advancements** grid grouped by category with locked/unlocked styling, and a **Statistics** list of the counters. Each unlock raises an _"Advancement Unlocked"_ toast and a celebratory chime
  - **Persist across death.** Like `xp` and unlike status `effects`, both stats and advancements are a long-term record that survives a death (`clearEffects` never touches them) and a reload
  - **Architecture**: one observer at the engine's single `emit` chokepoint folds every gameplay event into the stat counters (`recordEvent`), then unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed and announces it (`advancementUnlocked` event) — no per-system bookkeeping. The whole set is a **declarative registry** in `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts` (`{ stat, threshold }` per row), so `evaluateAdvancements` is pure and adding one is a one-line edit. A new broadly-useful `crafted` event drives the craft/brew/trade counters; `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) is the single source of truth for counting hostile kills. The overlay reads detail through a new `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render, so play never churns the snapshot with stat values the HUD doesn't show

## [0.11.0] - 2026-06-28

### Fixed

- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)

input.prompt:
Explore the voxel game repo at /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript). Search breadth: medium. I'm evaluating candidate next features and need feasibility facts about worldgen, dimensions, and the renderer. Answer precisely, with file paths:

1. Dimension machinery (recently shipped Nether): is the dimension type a closed two-value union ("overworld" | "nether") or extensible? Where is it defined, and how many places would need touching to add a THIRD dimension (save `dimensions` section, portal routing, renderer environment profiles, online dimension shards in server/)? Is portal destination hardcoded overworld<->nether?
2. Biomes: how are biomes defined (lib/world/generation.ts?), how many exist, and how hard is adding a new surface biome (e.g. desert or ice) — is there a biome registry/table or interleaved code? What's WORLDGEN_VERSION currently?
3. Nether interior: does the nether generator place any STRUCTURES (fortress-like), or only caverns/ore/glowstone/lava? Where's the nether generation code?
4. Boss/endgame: where does the Dragon Lord boss fight live (summoned via Cursed Totem)? Is it fought in the overworld? Anything referencing an "End"-like finale?
5. Maps/minimap: what does the minimap render (where), and was full map-item rendering ever stubbed? 
6. Renderer environment profiles: where are per-dimension sky/fog/light profiles defined (from the nether work) — is adding another profile trivial?
7. Multiplayer dimension shards (server/): how does the server decide which dimensions exist for a room — is it keyed generically by dimension id or hardcoded overworld+nether?
8. Current versions: save schema version, WORLDGEN_VERSION, protocol version (check lib/game/save.ts or similar, and server/ protocol file).

Return a compact factual summary — no code dumps, just findings with paths.

content.text:
Here are the findings, all paths absolute.

## 1. Dimension machinery — CLOSED two-value union, not extensible
- **Type def:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/types.ts:365` — `export type DimensionId = "overworld" | "nether";` A closed string union.
- Adding a THIRD dimension touches at minimum these places (several are hardcoded, not generic):
  1. `lib/game/types.ts:365` — the union itself.
  2. `lib/game/types.ts:451` — `SaveData.dimensions?: { nether?: DimensionSection }` — the save section is a hardcoded object with a literal `nether` key, not `Partial<Record<DimensionId, …>>`. Must be widened.
  3. `lib/game/save.ts:330` — `VALID_DIMENSIONS: Record<DimensionId, true> = { overworld: true, nether: true }` (compile-error guard, good) and `dimensionSectionOf` (save.ts:322) has an `overworld ? top-level : dimensions?.[dim]` branch that already generalizes for non-overworld.
  4. `lib/net/protocol.ts:250` — `isDimension = (v) => v === "overworld" || v === "nether"` — hardcoded wire validator.
  5. `lib/game/render/dimensionProfiles.ts:28` — `DIMENSION_PROFILES: Record<DimensionId, DimensionProfile>` (compile-error keyed — adding a key is forced/trivial).
  6. `server/room.ts` — see #7; shards Map is generic but the nether lifecycle is hardcoded.
  7. `lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.ts` — per-dimension spawn tables gated `if (state.dimension === "nether")` (lines 120, 189, 291).
- **Portal destination is hardcoded binary:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/portal.ts:206` — `target: state.dimension === "nether" ? "overworld" : "nether"`. A pure toggle; there is no destination map/routing table. Only one portal block type exists (`BlockId.NetherPortal`).

## 2. Biomes — 5, split across an enum + interleaved gen code (no single registry)
- **Enum:** `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/blocks.ts:152` `BiomeId { Plains, Desert, Ocean, Forest, Mountains }` — 5 biomes.
- **Classification** (thresholds, interleaved if-chain): `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts:85` `getBiome()`.
- **Height/tree table:** `lib/world/generation.ts:23` `GEN.biomes` per-biome `{baseHeight, noiseScale, treeChance}`, plus a parallel `BIOME_IDS` array (generation.ts:96) and a second `ISLANDS_BIOMES` table (generation.ts:113) that must be kept in sync.
- **Surface block choice** is interleaved: `generation.ts:216` an `if (biome === Desert || Ocean) Sand … else if Mountains … Snow/Stone` chain.
- Adding a biome (e.g. Ice) touches: the enum, `getBiome` thresholds, `GEN.biomes` + `BIOME_IDS` + `ISLANDS_BIOMES`, the surface-block if-chain, and optionally audio (`lib/game/audio/musicBrain.ts:42`, `audioDirector.ts`). Because it changes generated bytes it forces a **WORLDGEN_VERSION bump** and re-baselining (`lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`, `generation.test.ts`). No registry/data-table abstraction — it is interleaved code in ~4 files.
- **WORLDGEN_VERSION = 11** (`lib/game/config.ts:428`).

## 3. Nether interior — NO structures, only terrain/ore/hazard
- Code: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`. `generateNetherWorld` (line 55) runs exactly: `fillNetherMass` (netherrack + bedrock caps), `carveNetherCaverns` (worm tunnels + sea chambers), `floodLavaSea`, `placeGlowstoneClusters`, `placeBlaziteOre`, `sealBedrockCaps`. There is **no fortress/structure pass** — no rooms, no loot placement, no bridges. A fortress-like structure would be a wholly new generation pass.

## 4. Boss / endgame — fought in the overworld; no "End" dimension
- Summon: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:1644` `trySummonBoss` — from a held `boss_summoner` ("Cursed Totem", `lib/game/items.ts:368`), spawns at `randomLandPointNear(... player.position ...)` (surface land near the player). Not dimension-gated in code, but it seeks a land surface point and the totem is diamond-gated overworld play — effectively an **overworld** fight.
- Spawn helper: `lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.ts:70` `spawnBoss`. Config `BOSS_*` at `lib/game/config.ts:184-196` (HP 1000).
- Drop `dragon_heart` → crafts `dragon_sword` (`lib/game/recipes.ts:742`, `lib/game/mobLoot.ts:63`). Advancement `dragon_slayer` (`advancements.ts:205`). Finale UI: `components/game/VictoryScreen.tsx`, `components/game/BossHealthBar.tsx`.
- **No "End"-like dimension or finale zone exists** — the endgame is the in-overworld Dragon Lord + VictoryScreen. Only `overworld` and `nether` dimensions exist.

## 5. Maps / minimap
- Minimap: `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/minimap.ts` — a top-right 144px canvas rendering top-down column colors around the player via `columnColor(world, x, z, isNether)` (`lib/game/render/minimapColors.ts`), plus a player yaw arrow. It is **dimension-aware** (minimap.ts:55).
- The only "map" item is `treasure_map` (`lib/game/items.ts:365`); holding it overlays red-X markers for unlooted buried-treasure sites on the minimap (minimap.ts:92-107). There is **no separate full-screen map item, and no evidence a full map-item renderer was ever stubbed** — grep for map/stub/TODO/placeholder turned up nothing map-related beyond `treasure_map`.

## 6. Renderer environment profiles — trivial to extend
- `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/dimensionProfiles.ts` — `DIMENSION_PROFILES: Record<DimensionId, DimensionProfile>` with `overworld` and `nether` entries. Fields: `daySky, nightSky, fogNear, fogFar, skyLightFloor, celestials, precipitation`. Because it's a `Record<DimensionId, …>`, adding a dimension **forces** a new entry at compile time — adding a profile is trivial. Note: comment (lines 3-8) says these are **construction-time constants** — `skyLightFloor` is baked into the shader source string, so swap-on-travel rebuilds the renderer; no live uniform switching. Consumed by `lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts`.

## 7. Multiplayer dimension shards (server/) — MOSTLY generic, nether lifecycle hardcoded
- `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/server/room.ts`. The shard container is generic: `shards = new Map<DimensionId, DimensionShard>()` (room.ts:178), `ensureShard(dimension)` boots any dimension's engine on demand (room.ts:273), `travelPlayer` (room.ts:322) hands players between shards by id, `shardOf`/`broadcastToDimension` are generic.
- BUT the **eviction/persistence lifecycle is hardcoded to nether**: `dormantNether` (room.ts:193), `netherEmptySinceMs`/`netherLingerMs` (194-196), `sweepNetherShard()` (room.ts:372, literally `this.shards.get("nether")` / `shards.delete("nether")`), and `composeSave()` (room.ts:301) special-cases `save.dimensions?.nether` and `this.shards.get("nether")`. Overworld is always constructed at boot (room.ts:224). So: keyed generically for *simulation and travel*, but a third online dimension would need its own dormant-section + linger-evict + compose-save wiring (or a generalization of those three).

## 8. Current versions
- **Save schema version: 18** — `SaveData.version: 18` (`lib/game/types.ts:449`); migration chain v1→v18 in `lib/game/save.ts` (latest `migrateSaveV17toV18`, save.ts:288). The `dimensions` section and `worldgenVersion` stamp were added at v18.
- **WORLDGEN_VERSION = 11** — `lib/game/config.ts:428`.
- **PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4** — `lib/net/protocol.ts:28`.

One cross-cutting note for feature-sizing: worldgen is byte-pinned by SHA-256 baselines (`lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`, `netherGeneration.test.ts`), and a single WORLDGEN_VERSION stamp governs BOTH dimensions' diffs — any change to overworld or nether generation (new biome, nether fortress) bumps that one version and discards all dimensions' stored block-diffs on load (`applyWorldgenGuard`, save.ts:302).

Highest assigned id is `BlaziteOre = 94` (line 149). **Next free id = 95.** Ids are dense 0–94 with no gaps. `BiomeId` is a separate enum starting at 0 (line 152), unrelated to the block-id space.

## 2. Dropped items — straight to inventory, no ground entities
Drops never become world entities. There is no `ItemEntity`/`DroppedItem`/ground-item type anywhere in `lib/` or `server/` (grep confirms zero hits).
- Mining: `lib/game/engine/systems/mining.ts:70-71` — `rollBlockDrops(...)` then `adjustSlotCount(player.inventory, ...)` directly.
- Mob death: `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:1606-1631` (`removeMobAt`) — `rollMobDrops` (from `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`) then `adjustSlotCount(receiver.inventory, ...)`. Line 1630 comment: "Drops land straight in inventory (no ground item)". Fishing (`fishing.ts:44`) is the same pattern.
- **Hopper/item-automation feasibility:** there is no ground-item entity abstraction at all, so item-on-ground physics, pickup radius, and its replication would all be net-new. Big lift.

## 3. Vehicle system
- `VehicleKind = "raft" | "ship" | "minecart"` at `lib/game/types.ts:127`. `VehicleState` at `lib/game/engine/state.ts:222` (id/kind/position/yaw/rider/optional `speed`). Logic: `lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts`; visuals `lib/game/render/vehicleVisuals.ts`.

Movement: minecart is rail-guided (`moveMinecartAlongRails`, throttle/boost/friction, powered rails); boats free-steer on water (`tickVehicles`). Placement: `tryPlaceVehicle` — boats require a water surface, carts require a rail.
- **Land vehicle / rideable mob: neither exists.** Every vehicle is hard-gated to water or rail via `vehicleHasSupport`/`canOccupy` (vehicles.ts:128-157) — there is no free-ground movement branch. `MobState` (state.ts:116) has **no rider/mount field**; all mount plumbing lives on `player.mountedVehicleId` + `VehicleState.rider`. A rideable horse would require either a new `VehicleKind` plus a new "ground support" branch in `vehicleHasSupport`/`canOccupy`, or adding mount plumbing to `MobState` from scratch. - **Multiplayer:** vehicles replicate. `VehiclePose` (`lib/net/protocol.ts:149`) is sent as per-tick deadbanded deltas (`vp`, protocol:206) and in the full `WorldSyncMessage.vehicles` (protocol:138-139). ## 4. Mob status effects — none

## 5. Damage seam — bare amount, no attacker
The player-damage path carries only a number.
- `damageCombat = (player, amount)` at `GameEngine.ts:1519` → `applyDamageWithArmor(player, amount, rng)` (`lib/game/engine/systems/playerLife.ts:14`).

## 6. Player status effects + renderer/detection seams
- Core: `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts`. Each effect is read by exactly one seam (movement, melee, mining, environmental gates). HUD: `components/game/ActiveEffects.tsx`. Applied by potions via `ItemEffect` (types.ts:15).
- **Night Vision (brightness): no per-player seam yet.** Renderer brightness is global, derived only from `state.daylight` (`lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts:642-648`, `sun.intensity`/`hemiLight.intensity`); there is no per-player brightness uniform. You'd add a new `EffectId` and pipe a brightness boost into `GameRenderer`.
- **Invisibility / mob detection:** the single aggro chokepoint is `nearestTargetablePlayer` (`lib/game/engine/players.ts:123`), which every hunting mob calls to pick a target (already filters `isDead` and `mobsThreaten(gameMode)`). Adding an invisibility check there hides the player from all aggro in one place. Per-mob sight distance is `MobState.detectRange` (state.ts:148), consumed in `mobAI.ts` (`acquireTarget`, ~line 110). ## 7. Projectiles (arrows vs spears) + splash-potion feasibility
- Arrows: spawn in `lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts` (`spawnArrow`), flight/hit in `lib/game/engine/systems/projectileAI.ts` (`tickProjectiles`). `ProjectileState` state.ts:169; visuals `projectileVisuals.ts`. **Replicated** (`ProjectilePose` protocol:156, `prj` deltas).
- Spears: `lib/game/engine/systems/spears.ts` (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`/`tickThrownSpears`). `ThrownSpearState` state.ts:198; visuals `spearVisuals.ts`. **Not replicated** — no "spear" anywhere in `lib/net/` (SP-only today).
- **Shared machinery:** the two use the *same hit primitives* (`voxelRaycast` for terrain + a manual segment/closest-point-vs-mob-cylinder sweep) but share **no code** — separate state arrays, tick loops, and spawn functions. There is no common projectile base to extend.
- **AoE-on-impact:** nothing like it exists for projectiles. The only radial-damage code is the explosion system `lib/game/engine/systems/explosion.ts` (radial falloff vs players + TNT). A splash potion would be a third parallel thrown system: model the arc on `spears.ts`, and on impact do a radial mob/player scan (pattern from `explosion.ts`) calling `addEffect` (statusEffects.ts) instead of damage. Moderate lift — copy-the-pattern, not plug-in — and you'd need to add net replication if it should be visible in multiplayer.

## 8. Redstone-lite + piston feasibility
- Sim: `lib/game/engine/systems/redstone.ts` (`tickRedstone`); block-graph helpers in `lib/world/redstone.ts` and rail helpers in `lib/world/rails.ts`. `RedstoneState` (cells/buttonTimers/prevDoorPowered/timer) created in redstone.ts:44.
- Components (BlockId pairs off/on, blocks.ts:58-74): RedstoneWire 58/59, Lever 60/61, Button 62/63, PressurePlate 64/65, RedstoneTorch 66/67 (inverter), RedstoneLamp 68/69, PoweredRail 70/71, DetectorRail 72/73, plain Rail 74. Doors and TNT are downstream consumers.
- Model: binary power, fixed cadence (`REDSTONE_TICK_SECONDS`), the whole tracked cell-set is re-derived from the block grid each pass; wire relaxes outward up to `REDSTONE_WIRE_RANGE` hops with 1-block slope climb. Every effect is a block-id swap through `blockChanges.set` (relight + save-diff + net-journal for free). Plates/detector rails read `collectOccupiedCells` (players + mobs + minecarts).
- **Moving-block machinery for pistons: none.** Redstone only swaps ids in place; the only thing that physically moves relative to the grid is the minecart (`vehicles.ts` rail-follow). There is no displaced/pushed-block entity, animation, or collision. Pistons would need entirely new moving-block machinery that does not exist anywhere.
- **Online:** server-side only. Redstone (and all world systems) early-return on replicas; clients receive the resulting block deltas via the tick journal like any other edit (see redstone.ts header, lines 38-41). Riderless minecart coasting is likewise server-owned (`tickCoastingMinecarts`, vehicles.ts:314).

Design an implementation plan for the next feature epic in the voxel game repo at /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft (Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript strict + Three.js + Bun; zero binary assets — everything generated from code).

# The feature: "Nether fortresses + worldgen batch"

Two bundled worldgen changes under ONE WORLDGEN_VERSION bump (11→12), since a single stamp governs both dimensions' block diffs and any bump discards players' block edits (established policy — bundle to avoid two discards):

1. **Nether fortress structures**: the Nether currently generates only caverns/lava seas/glowstone/blazite (lib/world/netherGeneration.ts: fillNetherMass, carveNetherCaverns, floodLavaSea, placeGlowstoneClusters, placeBlaziteOre, sealBedrockCaps — NO structures, NO loot). Add a fortress-like structure pass: nether-brick construction (new block ids from 95), corridors/bridges/rooms, loot chests, giving players a reason to explore beyond mining.
2. **Redstone ore worldgen (overworld)**: redstone dust is currently crafted (1 gold ore + 1 coal → 8) because ore worldgen was explicitly deferred "to a future worldgen batch" when redstone-lite shipped. Add deep-overworld RedstoneOre; ore drops dust (Fortune-eligible via FORTUNE_ORE_BLOCKS in the enchantment seams).

# Established repo conventions you MUST design within

- **Worldgen determinism**: every seed-determined pass must use the portable noise/PRNG primitives in lib/world/noise.ts (byte-identical across JS engines — a Bun server and browser clients worldgen independently and must agree). Each new pass gets its OWN decoupled PRNG stream with a FRESH xor seed constant (history: coal and village once collided on 0x85ebca6b — never reuse constants). # Implementation plan: Nether fortresses + worldgen batch (WORLDGEN_VERSION 11→12)

**Branch:** `feat/worldgen-v12-fortress-redstone`

One bump covers both changes — `applyWorldgenGuard` (`lib/game/save.ts:302`) discards every dimension's diffs on a stamp mismatch, so bundling avoids two discards. Save schema stays v18, protocol stays v4.

## Key architectural findings that shaped the design

1. **The nether derive-vs-build problem is different from the overworld's.** In `GameEngine.ts` the `collect*Sites` calls (lines 329–335) run on the freshly regenerated world *after* `generateNetherWorld` but *before* `applySavedChanges` — so `collectFortressSites` would see a world that already contains fortresses. Dungeons solve derive/build lockstep with seed-pure `terrainTopY`; the nether has no seed-pure surface (caverns are PRNG-carved). Therefore **fortress placement must read zero blocks**: acceptance is a pure function of the PRNG draws (fixed draw count per attempt, the `buildDungeons` invariant), and the structure is *imposed* — it carves its own interior through netherrack/air/lava alike.
2. **The redstone ore pass runs LAST (repo policy) — which creates a new hazard the existing ores never faced**: `placeOres` replaces Stone *and* Cobblestone, but runs before `placeDungeons`/`placeVillages`. A last-running ore pass would eat dungeon walls and village paths (both cobble). So redstone ore **replaces `BlockId.Stone` only**.
3. **The spawner's mob kind is hardcoded, not per-site** (`SPAWNER_KINDS = ["zombie","skeleton","spider"]`, `spawnDirector.ts:311`, loop over `dungeonSpawnerIndices` only at :334). Reuse is a small refactor: iterate the union of dungeon + fortress spawner sets, pick the kind list by set membership (`["imp","imp","scorcher"]` for fortress, mirroring the nether ambient `spawnKinds` at :291).
4. **One extra hash pin is easy to miss**: `generation.test.ts:520` pins an in-region **meshing snapshot** digest over generated terrain — redstone ore re-rolls it along with the 7 overworld world digests. The Chromium e2e (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts:36`) imports `WORLDGEN_BASELINES` so it follows the re-baseline with no edits.
5. **`itemSources.ts` priority is hunt > craft > mine** — so the dust hint only changes if the gold+coal recipe is retired (decision left to you; a `MINE_OVERRIDES["redstone"] = "Mine redstone ore"` entry is needed only in that branch, else the auto hint reads "Mine Redstone Dust").
6. **PRNG constants in use** (never reuse): 0x85ebca6b (coal *and* village — the historical collision, still live), 0x9e3779b9 (dungeon), 0xc2b2ae35 (shipwreck), 0x27d4eb2f (treasure), 0x94d049bb / 0x3c6ef372 (nether caverns/ore), cell salts 0x51ed2701/0x2ab7de19, loot families 0x9e3779b1/0x68e31da4/0x94d049bb. **Fresh, verified-unused picks:** `0x7f4a7c15` (fortress placement), `0x165667b1` (redstone ore pass), `0xbf58476d` (fortress loot family).

## New blocks (append-only)

- `NetherBrick = 95`, `RedstoneOre = 96` in the `blocks.ts` const enum + `BLOCK_COLORS`/`HELD_BLOCK_COLORS` entries (NetherBrick dark maroon ~[0.25,0.11,0.12]; RedstoneOre stone-gray like all ores).
- `atlas.ts`: two paint branches — mortar-grid seams for NetherBrick (the Chest-grain approach), red flecks `n > 0.85 → tone([0.85,0.15,0.1],1)` for RedstoneOre (the RubyOre pattern).
- `items.ts`: `nether_brick` ITEM_DEF; `BLOCK_TO_SLOT[RedstoneOre] = "redstone"` (drops the existing dust item directly — the CoalOre pattern, no ore-block item); add to `FORTUNE_ORE_BLOCKS` (line 552); `BREAK_HARDNESS` NetherBrick 6, RedstoneOre 8.
- `mining.ts canMineBlock`: NetherBrick `toolTier >= 1`; RedstoneOre `toolTier >= 3` — the sliver pickaxe's mineTier is 3 (`items.ts:183`), the iron-equivalent gate, same as Ruby/Gold ore.
- `xp.ts ORE_XP[RedstoneOre] = 3`; `advancements.ts MINED_STAT_BY_BLOCK` → `"redstone_ore_mined"`.
- Recipe: furnace `1 Netherrack -> 1 Nether Brick` (keeps the material renewable/buildable).

## Redstone ore pass (generation.ts)

- `GEN.redstoneOreConfig: { attempts: 12000, minY: 2, maxY: 24, minSize: 4, maxSize: 8 }` — an explicit deep band (unlike the loose maxYOffset scheme), coal-style embedded walk (no air-adjacency gate), Stone-only replacement, own mulberry32 stream `seed ^ 0x165667b1`, appended after `placeBuriedTreasure` as the final call in `generateWorld`. Every earlier pass stays byte-identical; seed-pure `collect*` derivations can't shift. Attempts need tuning before re-baselining (the confined band makes hit rates far higher than the other ores').

## Fortress algorithm (netherGeneration.ts)

`NETHER_GEN` additions: `fortressCount: 10` (area-scaled via `scaledByArea`), `fortressMinSeparation: 64`, `fortressMinSpawnDistance: 40`, `fortressBaseY: 40` (lavaSeaLevel+8, so bridges cross the seas). Per attempt, draw ~11 randoms up front (cx, cz, 4 arm lengths, 4 chest rolls, spawner roll) regardless of acceptance; reject on spawn proximity, bounds, or separation from already-accepted sites (all PRNG-pure). Structure per accepted site:

- **Central keep**: 11×11 nether-brick shell, floor pad at baseY−1, 4-high walls with `cellHash01`-gated window gaps (position-hashed — consumes no stream), 9×9×4 carved interior, Glowstone in the interior ceiling corners (self-lighting via the normal bake). One guaranteed chest at a fixed offset, second on roll<0.5, `Spawner` at center on roll<0.75.
- **Four bridges** (N/E/S/W): 3-wide walkway, 1-high railings, 3-high air carved above, length 12–24 clamped to bounds.
- **End towers**: 7×7 room per arm end, chest on roll<0.6.
- All writes clamp `y ∈ [2, sizeY−8]` and spare Bedrock. Insert `placeNetherFortresses` after `placeBlaziteOre`, before `sealBedrockCaps` (caps stay the final defensive pass; all earlier passes stay byte-identical).
- Export `FortressSites = { chestIndices, spawnerIndices }` + `collectFortressSites(world)` (the write-flag + sink replay, exactly `buildDungeonRoom`'s pattern); re-export via `lib/world/index.ts`.

## Engine wiring

- `state.ts`: `fortressChestIndices`/`fortressSpawnerIndices` Sets + `{ type: "fortressLooted" }` GameEvent.
- `GameEngine.ts` (~329–335, ~422): nether dimension collects fortress sites (overworld gets empties — the inverse of today's dungeon/shipwreck lines). Runs identically on server shards and replicas; `lootedWorldgenChests` already persists per-dimension (`DimensionSection.lootedChests`, types.ts:434) and rides worldSync (`NetworkSession.ts:447`) — **no save/protocol change, and nothing extra for online**.
- `lib/game/fortressLoot.ts` (new): `FORTRESS_LOOT` tiers via the shared `rollTieredLoot`. Common: nether_brick 2–6 (guaranteed non-empty), glowstone_dust, gold_ore, coal, bread; rare: blazite_ore, obsidian (thematic portal-repair kit), diamond_ore, sapphire_sword, redstone dust 4–8 (ties the batch together).
- `dungeon.ts fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: fortress branch → `rollFortressLoot(seededRng((seed ^ idx ^ 0xbf58476d) >>> 0))` + emit `fortressLooted`. Both existing call sites (interact.ts:122, mining.ts:83) need no change; the shared looted-set closes the re-roll exploit for the new family automatically.
- `advancements.ts`: `fortress_looted` stat (recordEvent case + STATS row) and Adventure row `fortress_raider` ("Loot a chest in a nether fortress", icon `nether_brick`) — the exact `treasureUnearthed`/`x_marks_the_spot` pattern.
- `config.ts:428` → `WORLDGEN_VERSION = 12` + history comment.

## Commit slices (each lint-green, Conventional Commits)

1. `feat(world): nether brick and redstone ore blocks (ids 95–96)` — blocks/atlas/items/mining/xp/advancement-counter/recipe + tests. Zero worldgen writes; all digests provably untouched.
2. `feat(world): redstone ore worldgen + WORLDGEN_VERSION 12 (overworld re-baseline)` — generation.ts pass, config bump, re-pin 7 overworld digests in `generationBaselines.ts` **and the meshing snapshot at generation.test.ts:520**, new structural probe (ore present, ≤ maxY, never in cobble structures); all pre-existing probes must pass unchanged.
3. `feat(world): nether fortress generation (nether re-baseline)` — netherGeneration.ts + index.ts export, re-pin 4 nether digests, probes: ≥1 fortress at 128²/seed 1337; every nether Chest ∈ `collectFortressSites` (port of the overworld chest-census probe); chest/spawner indices hold the right blocks; derive determinism (collect twice ≡); sites clear of center; keep interiors walkable; 64² tiny worlds still boot.
4. `feat(engine): fortress loot chests, spawners, and the Fortress Raider advancement` — fortressLoot.ts(+test), state.ts, GameEngine.ts, dungeon.ts, spawnDirector.ts, advancements.ts; engine test boots a small `dimension: "nether"` engine, opens a fortress chest, asserts one-time fill + advancement; spawner drips imp/scorcher; re-run `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`.
5. `feat(game): redstone dust sourcing` — recipe fate per your decision (see below).
6. `docs: worldgen v12 — nether fortresses + redstone ore` — CHANGELOG [Unreleased] (flagging the bump discards both dimensions' edits), manual.md ("Surviving the Nether"), reference.md (Blocks + a "Nether fortresses" section beside Dungeons/Shipwrecks + loot/recipe tables), tuning.md (new GEN/NETHER_GEN constants, hash-pinned flag), testing.md (coverage rows + v11→v12 re-baseline history entry), save-format.md (no schema bump; new loot family on the existing `lootedChests`).

## Test plan summary

Unit per slice; 8 world digests + 1 meshing pin re-baselined across slices 2–3 (harvest from failing runs, record in testing.md — the documented policy); all pre-existing structural probes must survive untouched; Chromium determinism e2e follows the constants with no edits; **no new e2e** (renderer touched only by two procedural atlas branches; online needs nothing — sites re-derive from seed everywhere, chest fill is already engine-side); one manual browser smoke (walk a fortress, loot, toast).

## Decisions left for you

1. **Redstone dust recipe fate**: keep gold+coal as a renewable fallback (recipe-book hint stays "Craft it") vs retire it (hint becomes "Mine redstone ore" via a new MINE_OVERRIDES entry; ore is finite and sliver-gated so early circuits get later). Middle path: keep but nerf 8→4 dust.
2. **Fortress guardian MobKind** (severable, ~1 day): must fill MOB_TEMPLATES, FACTION_BY_KIND, MOB_DROPS, MOB_XP, CALL_INTERVALS, MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS, MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS, MOB_LABELS (itemSources), HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS + MobKind union + model + spawn wiring — TS exhaustiveness makes it mechanical but wide.
3. **Nether-brick slabs/stairs** (severable, ~half day): ids 97–101, extends slabs.ts material tables; craft-only, so keep the fortress full-cube to keep this severable from the hash bump.
4. **Fortress loot exclusive** (severable, ~half day): one additive item id in the rare tier — needs a design pick (brewing ingredient vs gear component).
5. Tuning defaults (fortressCount 10, spawner 75% roll, ore attempts 12000) are proposals — settle before the re-baseline commits land.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/netherGeneration.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/generation.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/dungeon.ts
- /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/world/generationBaselines.ts
