# Nether fortresses + worldgen batch (WORLDGEN_VERSION 11→12)

## Context

The Nether epic (v0.16.0 + online shards, PR #62) shipped, but the dimension is content-thin: `lib/world/netherGeneration.ts` generates only caverns, lava seas, glowstone, and blazite ore — no structures, no loot, no reason to explore beyond mining. Separately, redstone-lite deliberately deferred redstone-ore worldgen "to a future worldgen batch" (dust is crafted from 1 gold ore + 1 coal as a stopgap).

This epic pays off both in **one** WORLDGEN_VERSION bump (11→12): a single stamp governs both dimensions' block diffs (`applyWorldgenGuard`, `lib/game/save.ts:302`), so bundling avoids discarding players' block edits twice. Save schema stays **v18**, protocol stays **v4**.

**User-decided scope** (2026-07-10): retire the gold+coal dust recipe (ore becomes the sole source); guard fortresses with spawners of existing imps/scorchers (no new MobKind); **include** nether-brick slab/stair variants; **no** fortress-exclusive loot item.

**Branch:** `feat/worldgen-v12-fortress-redstone` (epic-scale → branch + PR per AGENTS.md).

## Key constraints (verified in code)

- **Determinism**: all passes use portable primitives from `lib/world/noise.ts`; each new pass gets its own decoupled PRNG stream with a **fresh** xor constant. In use: `0x85ebca6b` (coal+village), `0x9e3779b9`, `0xc2b2ae35`, `0x27d4eb2f`, `0x94d049bb`, `0x3c6ef372`, `0x51ed2701`, `0x2ab7de19`, `0x9e3779b1`, `0x68e31da4`. **Fresh picks:** `0x7f4a7c15` (fortress placement), `0x165667b1` (redstone ore), `0xbf58476d` (fortress loot family).
- **Fortress placement must read zero blocks**: site collection (`GameEngine.ts:329–335`) runs on the regenerated world *after* structures exist, and the nether has no seed-pure surface fn. Acceptance = pure function of PRNG draws (fixed draw count per attempt, the `buildDungeons` invariant); the structure is *imposed*, carving through netherrack/air/lava alike. `collectFortressSites(world)` re-derives by replaying the build with a write-flag sink (the `buildDungeonRoom` pattern).
- **Redstone ore replaces `BlockId.Stone` only** — it runs LAST (repo policy), after dungeons/villages, so replacing Cobblestone would eat their walls/paths.
- **Chest fill**: `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted` (`lib/game/engine/systems/dungeon.ts:26`) branches by site-set membership → loot table + family seed constant; all families share persisted `lootedWorldgenChests` (per-dimension via `DimensionSection.lootedChests`) — no save bump, no re-roll exploit, nothing extra for online (chest fill is engine/server-side; sites re-derive from seed on server and clients alike).
- **Spawner kind is hardcoded** (`SPAWNER_KINDS = ["zombie","skeleton","spider"]`, `spawnDirector.ts:311`; loops only `dungeonSpawnerIndices` at :334). Small refactor: iterate dungeon ∪ fortress spawner sets, pick kind list by set membership (`["imp","imp","scorcher"]` for fortress).
- **Hash pins to re-baseline**: 7 overworld digests + 4 nether digests (`lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`, `generation.test.ts`, `netherGeneration.test.ts`) **plus the meshing snapshot at `generation.test.ts:520`**. The Chromium determinism e2e imports `WORLDGEN_BASELINES` — follows automatically.

## New blocks & items

| Block | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NetherBrick | 95 | dark maroon; mortar-grid atlas paint (Chest-grain approach); hardness 6, toolTier ≥ 1; furnace recipe 1 Netherrack → 1 Nether Brick |
| RedstoneOre | 96 | stone-gray + red flecks (RubyOre pattern); hardness 8, **toolTier ≥ 3** (sliver pickaxe, like Ruby/Gold); drops existing `redstone` dust via `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` (CoalOre pattern); add to `FORTUNE_ORE_BLOCKS` (`items.ts:552`); `ORE_XP` 3; `MINED_STAT_BY_BLOCK` → `redstone_ore_mined` |
| NetherBrick slab + 4 stair facings | 97–101 | craft-only; extend the material tables in the existing slabs/stairs system (`lib/world/slabs.ts` et al., ids 75–89 precedent); recipes mirror plank/stone/cobble (3→6 slabs, 6→4 stairs) |

## Generation passes

**Redstone ore** (`lib/world/generation.ts`, appended as the final call in `generateWorld`): `GEN.redstoneOreConfig = { attempts: 12000, minY: 2, maxY: 24, minSize: 4, maxSize: 8 }` — explicit deep band, coal-style embedded walk, Stone-only replacement, mulberry32 stream `seed ^ 0x165667b1`. Tune attempts before re-baselining (confined band = higher hit rate than other ores).

**Fortresses** (`lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`, inserted after `placeBlaziteOre`, before `sealBedrockCaps`): `NETHER_GEN` additions `fortressCount: 10` (area-scaled), `fortressMinSeparation: 64`, `fortressMinSpawnDistance: 40`, `fortressBaseY: 40` (lava sea level + 8, bridges cross the seas). Per attempt draw ~11 randoms up front (cx, cz, 4 arm lengths, 4 chest rolls, spawner roll) regardless of acceptance; reject on spawn proximity/bounds/separation — all PRNG-pure. Per accepted site:
- **Central keep**: 11×11 nether-brick shell, floor pad at baseY−1, 4-high walls with `cellHash01`-gated window gaps (position-hashed, consumes no stream), glowstone in interior ceiling corners; 1 guaranteed chest + 1 at roll<0.5; `Spawner` at center at roll<0.75.
- **Four bridges** (N/E/S/W): 3-wide walkway, 1-high railings, 3-high carved clearance, length 12–24 clamped to bounds.
- **End towers**: 7×7 room per arm end, chest at roll<0.6.
- All writes clamp y ∈ [2, sizeY−8], spare Bedrock. Export `collectFortressSites` + re-export via `lib/world/index.ts`.

## Engine wiring

- `state.ts`: `fortressChestIndices`/`fortressSpawnerIndices` sets + `{ type: "fortressLooted" }` GameEvent.
- `GameEngine.ts` (~329–335): nether collects fortress sites; overworld gets empties (inverse of today's dungeon/shipwreck lines).
- New `lib/game/fortressLoot.ts` via shared `rollTieredLoot` — common: nether_brick 2–6 (guaranteed non-empty), glowstone_dust, gold_ore, coal, bread; rare: blazite_ore, obsidian, diamond_ore, sapphire_sword, redstone dust 4–8.
- `dungeon.ts`: fortress branch → `rollFortressLoot(seededRng((seed ^ idx ^ 0xbf58476d) >>> 0))` + emit `fortressLooted`. Existing call sites (`interact.ts:122`, `mining.ts:83`) unchanged.
- `advancements.ts`: `fortress_looted` stat + Adventure row `fortress_raider` ("Loot a chest in a nether fortress", icon `nether_brick`) — the `treasureUnearthed`/`x_marks_the_spot` pattern.
- `spawnDirector.ts`: spawner loop iterates both site sets; fortress spawners drip imp/imp/scorcher.
- **Dust sourcing**: delete the gold+coal recipe from `recipes.ts`; add `MINE_OVERRIDES["redstone"] = "Mine redstone ore"` in `itemSources.ts` (hint priority is hunt > craft > mine, so the override is required once the recipe is gone). Fix any recipe-count assertions/docs tables.
- `config.ts:428` → `WORLDGEN_VERSION = 12` + history comment.

## Commit slices (each lint-green, Conventional Commits, why in the body)

1. `feat(world): nether brick and redstone ore blocks (ids 95–96)` — blocks/atlas/items/mining/xp/advancement-counter/furnace recipe + tests. Zero worldgen writes; digests provably untouched.
2. `feat(world): redstone ore worldgen + WORLDGEN_VERSION 12` — generation pass, config bump, re-pin 7 overworld digests **+ meshing snapshot (`generation.test.ts:520`)**, structural probe (ore present, ≤ maxY, never inside cobble structures); all pre-existing probes pass unchanged.
3. `feat(world): nether fortress generation` — pass + `collectFortressSites`, re-pin 4 nether digests, probes: ≥1 fortress at 128²/seed 1337; every nether Chest ∈ collected sites; chest/spawner indices hold the right blocks; collect-twice determinism; sites respect spawn clearance; keep interiors walkable; 64² worlds still boot.
4. `feat(engine): fortress loot, spawners & the Fortress Raider advancement` — fortressLoot.ts(+test), state/GameEngine/dungeon/spawnDirector/advancements; engine test boots a small `dimension:"nether"` engine, opens a fortress chest, asserts one-time fill + advancement; spawner drips imp/scorcher; re-run `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`.
5. `feat(world): nether brick slabs and stairs (ids 97–101)` — material-table extension + recipes + tests; craft-only, no hash impact (fortress stays full-cube).
6. `feat(game): redstone dust comes from ore, not crafting` — recipe retired + hint override + test/docs-table fixes.
7. `docs: worldgen v12 — nether fortresses + redstone ore` — CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` (flag: the bump discards BOTH dimensions' block edits), manual.md ("Surviving the Nether"), reference.md (blocks + "Nether fortresses" section beside Dungeons/Shipwrecks + loot/recipe tables), tuning.md (new GEN/NETHER_GEN constants), testing.md (coverage rows + v11→v12 re-baseline history entry), save-format.md (no schema bump; new loot family on existing `lootedChests`), README if controls/quick-start touched (they aren't).

## Verification

- Per-commit: `bun run format` + `bun run lint` (per local-verify convention).
- Before PR (full gate): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (never gate on `bun test | tail` — exit 99 = passed-but-leaked), `bun run build`, **and local `bun run test:e2e`** (worldgen bytes change → determinism spec must pass with the re-baselined constants; CI runs e2e only on push-to-main, so local e2e is the PR gate; free port 3000 first / alt-port trick).
- Manual browser pass (before merge, lesson from the wolf/cat bug): portal into the Nether on a couple of seeds, find a fortress, walk a bridge, loot a chest (toast + advancement chime), watch a spawner drip imps, place nether-brick slabs/stairs, mine redstone ore with a sliver pickaxe (dust drops, Fortune applies), confirm the dust recipe is gone from the recipe book and the hint reads "Mine redstone ore".
- Open PR against `hutusi/monecraft` `main` only when the user asks; no AI-attribution lines.

# Nether fortresses + worldgen batch (WORLDGEN_VERSION 11→12)

## Context

The Nether epic (v0.16.0 + online shards, PR #62) shipped, but the dimension is content-thin: `lib/world/netherGeneration.ts` generates only caverns, lava seas, glowstone, and blazite ore — no structures, no loot, no reason to explore beyond mining. Separately, redstone-lite deliberately deferred redstone-ore worldgen "to a future worldgen batch" (dust is crafted from 1 gold ore + 1 coal as a stopgap).

This epic pays off both in **one** WORLDGEN_VERSION bump (11→12): a single stamp governs both dimensions' block diffs (`applyWorldgenGuard`, `lib/game/save.ts:302`), so bundling avoids discarding players' block edits twice. Save schema stays **v18**, protocol stays **v4**.

**User-decided scope** (2026-07-10): retire the gold+coal dust recipe (ore becomes the sole source); guard fortresses with spawners of existing imps/scorchers (no new MobKind); **include** nether-brick slab/stair variants; **no** fortress-exclusive loot item.

**Branch:** `feat/worldgen-v12-fortress-redstone` (epic-scale → branch + PR per AGENTS.md).

## Key constraints (verified in code)

- **Determinism**: all passes use portable primitives from `lib/world/noise.ts`; each new pass gets its own decoupled PRNG stream with a **fresh** xor constant. In use: `0x85ebca6b` (coal+village), `0x9e3779b9`, `0xc2b2ae35`, `0x27d4eb2f`, `0x94d049bb`, `0x3c6ef372`, `0x51ed2701`, `0x2ab7de19`, `0x9e3779b1`, `0x68e31da4`. **Fresh picks:** `0x7f4a7c15` (fortress placement), `0x165667b1` (redstone ore), `0xbf58476d` (fortress loot family).
- **Fortress placement must read zero blocks**: site collection (`GameEngine.ts:329–335`) runs on the regenerated world *after* structures exist, and the nether has no seed-pure surface fn. Acceptance = pure function of PRNG draws (fixed draw count per attempt, the `buildDungeons` invariant); the structure is *imposed*, carving through netherrack/air/lava alike. `collectFortressSites(world)` re-derives by replaying the build with a write-flag sink (the `buildDungeonRoom` pattern).
- **Redstone ore replaces `BlockId.Stone` only** — it runs LAST (repo policy), after dungeons/villages, so replacing Cobblestone would eat their walls/paths.
- **Chest fill**: `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted` (`lib/game/engine/systems/dungeon.ts:26`) branches by site-set membership → loot table + family seed constant; all families share persisted `lootedWorldgenChests` (per-dimension via `DimensionSection.lootedChests`) — no save bump, no re-roll exploit, nothing extra for online (chest fill is engine/server-side; sites re-derive from seed on server and clients alike).
- **Spawner kind is hardcoded** (`SPAWNER_KINDS = ["zombie","skeleton","spider"]`, `spawnDirector.ts:311`; loops only `dungeonSpawnerIndices` at :334). Small refactor: iterate dungeon ∪ fortress spawner sets, pick kind list by set membership (`["imp","imp","scorcher"]` for fortress).
- **Hash pins to re-baseline**: 7 overworld digests + 4 nether digests (`lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`, `generation.test.ts`, `netherGeneration.test.ts`) **plus the meshing snapshot at `generation.test.ts:520`**. The Chromium determinism e2e imports `WORLDGEN_BASELINES` — follows automatically.

## New blocks & items

| Block | Id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NetherBrick | 95 | dark maroon; mortar-grid atlas paint (Chest-grain approach); hardness 6, toolTier ≥ 1; furnace recipe 1 Netherrack → 1 Nether Brick |
| RedstoneOre | 96 | stone-gray + red flecks (RubyOre pattern); hardness 8, **toolTier ≥ 3** (sliver pickaxe, like Ruby/Gold); drops existing `redstone` dust via `BLOCK_TO_SLOT` (CoalOre pattern); add to `FORTUNE_ORE_BLOCKS` (`items.ts:552`); `ORE_XP` 3; `MINED_STAT_BY_BLOCK` → `redstone_ore_mined` |

## Generation passes

**Redstone ore** (`lib/world/generation.ts`, appended as the final call in `generateWorld`): `GEN.redstoneOreConfig = { attempts: 12000, minY: 2, maxY: 24, minSize: 4, maxSize: 8 }` — explicit deep band, coal-style embedded walk, Stone-only replacement, mulberry32 stream `seed ^ 0x165667b1`. Tune attempts before re-baselining (confined band = higher hit rate than other ores).

**Fortresses** (`lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`, inserted after `placeBlaziteOre`, before `sealBedrockCaps`): `NETHER_GEN` additions `fortressCount: 10` (area-scaled), `fortressMinSeparation: 64`, `fortressMinSpawnDistance: 40`, `fortressBaseY: 40` (lava sea level + 8, bridges cross the seas). export const WORLD_SIZE_X = 512;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Y = 150;
export const WORLD_SIZE_Z = 512;

export const enum BlockId {
  Air = 0,
  Grass = 1,
  Dirt = 2,
  Stone = 3,
  Wood = 4,
  Leaves = 5,
  Bedrock = 6,
  Planks = 7,
  Cobblestone = 8,
  Sand = 9,
  Brick = 10,
  Glass = 11,
  SliverOre = 12,
  RubyOre = 13,
  GoldOre = 14,
  SapphireOre = 15,
  DiamondOre = 16,
  Water = 17,
  Snow = 18,
  Cactus = 19,
  Bed = 20,
  Farmland = 21,
  // Wheat growth stages — consecutive ids so a crop advances by +1 (see randomTicks.ts).
  WheatStage0 = 22,
  WheatStage1 = 23,
  WheatStage2 = 24,
  WheatStage3 = 25,
  Furnace = 26,
  Chest = 27,
  // Dungeon blocks (worldgen-only flavor + the spawner block-entity marker).
  MossyCobblestone = 28,
  Spawner = 29,
  // Wood doors — 16 contiguous ids (4 facings × open/closed × lower/upper).
  // doors.ts derives state by offset from DoorNorthLower, so keep them in order.
  DoorNorthLower = 30,
  DoorNorthUpper = 31,
  DoorEastLower = 32,
  DoorEastUpper = 33,
  DoorSouthLower = 34,
  DoorSouthUpper = 35,
  DoorWestLower = 36,
  DoorWestUpper = 37,
  DoorNorthOpenLower = 38,
  DoorNorthOpenUpper = 39,
  DoorEastOpenLower = 40,
  DoorEastOpenUpper = 41,
  DoorSouthOpenLower = 42,
  DoorSouthOpenUpper = 43,
  DoorWestOpenLower = 44,
  DoorWestOpenUpper = 45,
  // A placeable light source: a solid block that emits block light (see lighting.ts).
  Torch = 46,
  // A worldgen-only hazard: a solid, unmineable block that emits max block light
  // and burns the player on contact (see lighting.ts, playerStats.ts).
  Lava = 47,
  // A shallow, common ore: mineable with a wood pickaxe, drops coal (furnace fuel).
  CoalOre = 48,
  // A placeable explosive: right-click with a torch to ignite a fuse, then it blows.
  Tnt = 49,
  // A young tree: plant on grass/dirt, grows into a tree over time (random ticks)
  // or instantly with bone meal. A solid cube like wheat (see atlas.ts).
  Sapling = 50,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open its brewing recipes (potions). Like
  // the furnace, it gates `station: "brewing"` recipes (see interact.ts).
  BrewingStand = 51,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the enchanting panel, where XP levels
  // are spent to enchant the held tool/weapon/armor (see interact.ts).
  EnchantingTable = 52,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the anvil panel, where XP levels are
  // spent to repair, combine, or rename the held gear (see interact.ts).
  Anvil = 53,
  // A crafted station: right-click to open the grindstone panel, which strips a
  // held item's enchantments and refunds some XP (see interact.ts).
  Grindstone = 54,
  // Ocean flora. Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (like wheat)
  // that generates in stalks on the ocean floor and grows upward through water
  // via random ticks; breaking one cell breaks the stalk above it (mining.ts).
  Kelp = 55,
  // Decorative reef blocks scattered on the ocean floor (worldgen only).
  CoralPink = 56,
  CoralBlue = 57,
  // Redstone-lite (see redstone.ts). Power state is id PARITY — even = off,
  // odd = on (`b | 1` / `b & ~1`) — so toggles ride the save diff like doors.
  // Ids 58-67 are floor-mounted "overlays": non-cube, non-colliding shapes
  // meshed via redstoneBounds. The lamp pair is a plain full cube.
  RedstoneWire = 58,
  RedstoneWireOn = 59,
  Lever = 60,
  LeverOn = 61,
  RedstoneButton = 62,
  RedstoneButtonOn = 63,
  PressurePlate = 64,
  PressurePlateOn = 65,
  // The torch item places the LIT variant; the power pass turns it off when
  // its support block is powered (the inverter rule).
  RedstoneTorchOff = 66,
  RedstoneTorch = 67,
  RedstoneLamp = 68,
  RedstoneLampOn = 69,
  // Rails (see rails.ts): flat floor overlays like wire, ridden by minecarts.
  // The powered/detector pairs join the redstone family — power is id PARITY,
  // so each pair MUST start on an even id. Plain Rail carries no power state
  // and must never pass through the redstoneOn/redstoneOff parity math.
  PoweredRail = 70,
  PoweredRailOn = 71,
  DetectorRail = 72,
  DetectorRailOn = 73,
  Rail = 74,
  // Partial building blocks (see slabs.ts). Slabs fill the bottom half of the
  // cell; stairs add a half-height back on the side they FACE, encoded as 4
  // contiguous ids per material (the doors offset-math precedent) in
  // north/east/south/west order — keep them contiguous and in order.
  PlankSlab = 75,
  StoneSlab = 76,
  CobbleSlab = 77,
  PlankStairsNorth = 78,
  PlankStairsEast = 79,
  PlankStairsSouth = 80,
  PlankStairsWest = 81,
  StoneStairsNorth = 82,
  StoneStairsEast = 83,
  StoneStairsSouth = 84,
  StoneStairsWest = 85,
  CobbleStairsNorth = 86,
  CobbleStairsEast = 87,
  CobbleStairsSouth = 88,
  CobbleStairsWest = 89,
  // Volcanic glass, created by quenching lava with a water bucket (interact.ts).
  // The hardest mineable block — diamond-pickaxe-gated (mining.ts) — and the
  // only material a nether portal frame can be built from (portal.ts).
  Obsidian = 90,
  // The lit portal surface filling an obsidian frame (portal.ts). Non-solid
  // (walked into, never collided with), unmineable (the solid raycast passes
  // through it — break the frame instead), emits light, and has no item.
  NetherPortal = 91,
  // The nether's landmass (netherGeneration.ts): a crimson rock, soft and
  // fast to mine — the dimension's building staple.
  Netherrack = 92,
  // Hanging crystal clusters on nether cavern ceilings: a strong natural
  // light source (see lighting.ts) that drops glowstone dust.
  Glowstone = 93,
  // The nether's deep ore, the post-diamond tier: diamond-pickaxe-gated,
  // smelts into blazite ingots (see recipes.ts).
  BlaziteOre = 94
}

up-front draws, which is what lets collectFortressSites() re-derive the

keeps two fortresses' longest opposing arms (2 x 35 = 70) from ever
touching, so no build can overwrite another's fixtures.

presence at 128^3/seed 1337, a chest/spawner census against the derived

/** Sound family of a block — drives break/place/footstep/mining-tick sounds. */
export type MaterialGroup = "stone" | "wood" | "grass" | "sand" | "glass" | "water";

export const MATERIAL_GROUPS: readonly MaterialGroup[] = ["stone", "wood", "grass", "sand", "glass", "water"];

// Exhaustive over BlockId so adding a block without a sound group is a type error.
const GROUP_BY_BLOCK: Record<BlockId, MaterialGroup> = {
  [BlockId.Air]: "grass", // never audible; mapped only for exhaustiveness

225	### Surviving the Nether
226	
227	The other side is a sealed world of **netherrack** caverns under a bedrock sky,
228	lit by hanging **glowstone** clusters and the glow of **lava seas** that fill
229	the deeps. There is no day, no weather, no water, and no mercy: **imps**
230	(fast, vicious melee brutes) and **scorchers** (hovering fire-spirits that lob
231	fireballs) spawn near you _constantly_ — the darkness that summons monsters
232	never lifts here. Come armed, wall yourself in when you mine, and consider a
233	Fire Resistance potion before working near the seas.
234	
235	Why go? Three exports. **Glowstone dust** (mine the ceiling clusters; 4 dust
236	recombine into a placeable glowstone block — a torch-strength light source for
237	your builds). **Blazite ore** — the post-diamond ore, found deep (below Y≈40)
238	and gated behind a diamond pickaxe like the obsidian you came through. Smelt 2
239	raw ore into a **blazite ingot** and forge the game's best craftable gear: the
240	**blazite pickaxe** (faster than diamond, and it chews obsidian), **sword**
241	(stronger than diamond, shy of the Dragon Sword), and **spear**. And bragging
242	rights: four advancements live down here.
243	
244	Your arrival portal is your lifeline home — its frame is ordinary obsidian, so
245	keep a spare flint & steel (and ideally frame material) on you. And know this
246	before you risk it: **dying in the Nether respawns you in the Nether**, at a
247	random cavern floor — your bed is a world away and can't reach you here. The
248	walk back to your (still lit, still glowing) portal is part of the price.
249	
250	### Rafts and ships
251	
252	Craft a **raft** (4 planks + 2 wood) or a **ship** (8 planks + 3 wood + 2 string)
253	to travel over water without swimming. Hold the vehicle and **right-click a water
254	surface** to place it. A raft is compact and slow; aim at it and right-click again
255	to board. A ship is larger and faster — step onto its deck and you board
256	automatically. While aboard, steer with the movement keys; crouch dismounts when
257	there is room beside the vehicle. Placing needs open water within reach — aim
258	somewhere that can't hold a boat, or once the world hits its 64-vehicle cap, and
259	you'll hear a dull "can't place here" thud instead. Rafts and ships appear in
260	their own **Vehicles** crafting category — alongside the land-going
261	[minecart](#rails-and-minecarts).
262	
263	### Hunger
264	
265	You have **20 hunger**, shown as **10 drumsticks**. Activity burns it:
266	
267	- ~1 hunger per **100 blocks sprinted**
268	- ~1 hunger per **300 blocks walked**
269	- ~1 hunger per **50 jumps**

### Surviving the Nether

The other side is a sealed world of **netherrack** caverns under a bedrock sky,
lit by hanging **glowstone** clusters and the glow of **lava seas** that fill
the deeps. There is no day, no weather, no water, and no mercy: **imps**
(fast, vicious melee brutes) and **scorchers** (hovering fire-spirits that lob
fireballs) spawn near you _constantly_ — the darkness that summons monsters
never lifts here. Come armed, wall yourself in when you mine, and consider a
Fire Resistance potion before working near the seas.

Why go? Three exports. **Glowstone dust** (mine the ceiling clusters; 4 dust
recombine into a placeable glowstone block — a torch-strength light source for
your builds). **Blazite ore** — the post-diamond ore, found deep (below Y≈40)
and gated behind a diamond pickaxe like the obsidian you came through. Smelt 2
raw ore into a **blazite ingot** and forge the game's best craftable gear: the
**blazite pickaxe** (faster than diamond, and it chews obsidian), **sword**
(stronger than diamond, shy of the Dragon Sword), and **spear**. And bragging
rights: four advancements live down here.

Your arrival portal is your lifeline home — its frame is ordinary obsidian, so
keep a spare flint & steel (and ideally frame material) on you. And know this
before you risk it: **dying in the Nether respawns you in the Nether**, at a
random cavern floor — your bed is a world away and can't reach you here. The
walk back to your (still lit, still glowing) portal is part of the price.

### Rafts and ships

Craft a **raft** (4 planks + 2 wood) or a **ship** (8 planks + 3 wood + 2 string)
to travel over water without swimming. Hold the vehicle and **right-click a water
surface** to place it. A raft is compact and slow; aim at it and right-click again
to board. A ship is larger and faster — step onto its deck and you board
automatically. While aboard, steer with the movement keys; crouch dismounts when
there is room beside the vehicle. Placing needs open water within reach — aim
somewhere that can't hold a boat, or once the world hits its 64-vehicle cap, and
you'll hear a dull "can't place here" thud instead. Rafts and ships appear in
their own **Vehicles** crafting category — alongside the land-going
[minecart](#rails-and-minecarts).

### Hunger

You have **20 hunger**, shown as **10 drumsticks**. Activity burns it:

- ~1 hunger per **100 blocks sprinted**
- ~1 hunger per **300 blocks walked**
- ~1 hunger per **50 jumps**

535	## Dungeons
536	
537	Small cobblestone rooms (speckled with mossy cobble) generate **underground**,
538	well clear of the spawn area. Each holds 1–2 **loot chests** and a central **mob
539	spawner**. The loot tables live in `lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`; a chest fills on
540	first open or break, with loot seeded so it's the same until you reach it.
541	
542	Each chest rolls a tier:
543	
544	| Tier   | Odds | Contents                                                                                                                      |
545	| ------ | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
546	| Common | 75%  | Bone (always), bread, cooked chicken, string, seeds, sliver/gold ore, an occasional stone pickaxe                             |
547	| Rare   | 25%  | Everything a common chest rolls **plus** diamond/sapphire ore, a ruby/sapphire sword, helmet/chestplate, rare diamond pickaxe |
548	
549	**Spawners** are time-independent: while you're within ~16 blocks, a spawner
550	drips one hostile (zombie/skeleton/spider) every ~8 s onto the room floor, up to
551	6 clustered nearby (and never past the global hostile cap of 16). Mining the
552	spawner block out stops it.
553	
554	## Shipwrecks
555	
556	Flooded plank hulls (broken walls, a snapped mast) sink onto the **deep ocean
557	floor**, clear of spawn. Each holds 1–2 loot chests filled lazily on first
558	access, exactly like dungeon chests but from their own table
559	(`lib/game/shipwreckLoot.ts`) — nautical salvage, and the main source of the
560	**treasure map**.
561	
562	| Tier   | Odds | Contents                                                                                       |
563	| ------ | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
564	| Common | 75%  | Planks (always), treasure map (40%), emeralds, string, leather, raw fish, dried kelp, gold ore |
565	| Rare   | 25%  | Everything a common chest rolls **plus** diamond/sapphire ore, a bow, a sapphire sword, boots  |
566	
567	## Buried treasure
568	
569	Lone chests buried **two blocks under beach sand** near the waterline, clear of
570	spawn. Hold a **treasure map** to see a compass pill (bearing + distance) to the
571	**nearest** unearthed chest and red **X** marks on the minimap; dig where X
572	marks the spot. The map is stateless — dig one up and the compass retargets to
573	the next. First access emits the **X Marks the Spot** advancement and rolls the
574	richest chest table in the game (`lib/game/buriedTreasureLoot.ts`).
575	
576	| Tier   | Odds | Contents                                                                                               |
577	| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
578	| Common | 75%  | Emeralds (always), gold/diamond/sapphire ore, cooked fish, arrows                                      |
579	| Rare   | 25%  | Everything a common chest rolls **plus** more diamonds, a gold sword, chestplate, rare diamond pickaxe |

593	  **victory screen**, and lets you craft the **Dragon Sword** (60 attack). You
594	  keep playing afterward; another totem summons it again.

## Nether fortresses

Nether-brick strongholds generate **in the Nether**: an 11×11 central keep with
four covered bridges spanning the lava-sea chambers, each ending in a 7×7
watchtower. The keep holds 1–2 **loot chests** and usually a **spawner** that
drips the nether's own hostiles (imps, the occasional scorcher — same rules as
dungeon spawners, and Peaceful keeps it inert); most towers hold a chest too.
Chests fill lazily on first access from their own table
(`lib/game/fortressLoot.ts`), and the first one you loot unlocks **Fortress
Raider**.

| Tier   | Odds | Contents                                                                                        |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Common | 75%  | Nether brick (always), glowstone dust, gold ore, coal, bread, redstone dust                     |
| Rare   | 25%  | Everything a common chest rolls **plus** blazite ore, obsidian, diamond ore, a sapphire sword   |

Obsidian in the rare tier is deliberate: it's a portal-repair kit for a raider
whose way home was griefed or mined out.

Why go? Three exports. **Glowstone dust** (mine the ceiling clusters; 4 dust
recombine into a placeable glowstone block — a torch-strength light source for
your builds). **Blazite ore** — the post-diamond ore, found deep (below Y≈40)
and gated behind a diamond pickaxe like the obsidian you came through. Smelt 2
raw ore into a **blazite ingot** and forge the game's best craftable gear: the
**blazite pickaxe** (faster than diamond, and it chews obsidian), **sword**
(stronger than diamond, shy of the Dragon Sword), and **spear**. And bragging
rights: four advancements live down here.

Why go? Four exports. **Glowstone dust** (mine the ceiling clusters; 4 dust
recombine into a placeable glowstone block — a torch-strength light source for
your builds). **Blazite ore** — the post-diamond ore, found deep (below Y≈40)
and gated behind a diamond pickaxe like the obsidian you came through. Smelt 2
raw ore into a **blazite ingot** and forge the game's best craftable gear: the

(stronger than diamond, shy of the Dragon Sword), and **spear**. **Fortress
loot** — see below. And bragging rights: five advancements live down here.

### Nether fortresses

Watch the horizon for dark **nether-brick** silhouettes: a walled keep whose
four covered bridges stride out over the lava seas to watchtowers. Fortresses
hold the Nether's **loot chests** — the keep usually 1–2 plus most towers one —
filled on first open like dungeon chests (nether brick salvage, glowstone dust,
gold, coal, bread, redstone dust; rarely blazite ore, **obsidian**, diamond
ore, or a sapphire sword). The catch: the keep usually houses a **spawner**
that drips imps (and the odd scorcher) while you're near — clear it or mine it
out before you shop. Your first fortress chest unlocks the **Fortress Raider**
advancement.

The brick itself is worth carrying home: smelt **1 netherrack → 1 nether
brick** in a furnace (no fuel needed) and craft its **slabs and stairs** — the
fortress look for your own builds.

100:The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 (under the fixture's `pauseOnBoot`, so no simulation step can edit a block before the hash) and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).
102:The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.
104:The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
106:The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.

Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.

To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.

The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 (under the fixture's `pauseOnBoot`, so no simulation step can edit a block before the hash) and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).

The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.

The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.

The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.

content.content:
30:- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
35:- `worldgenVersion` (optional) — the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stamped by `serialize()`. `applyWorldgenGuard` (`lib/game/save.ts`), run first thing in the `GameEngine` constructor (one seam covering single-player, cloud saves, and the server room), enforces the staleness rule: a **mismatched** stamp discards every dimension's world half (changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dimensions, villagesSeeded) and the world reboots from its seed with the players kept. An **absent** stamp (anything migrated from ≤ v17) is grandfathered untouched — the guard only ever acts on a stamp it wrote itself
36:- `dimensions` (optional) — non-overworld world halves, currently `{ nether?: DimensionSection }`. A `DimensionSection` carries exactly the world-half fields (`changes`, `blockEntities?`, `lootedChests?`, `mobs?`, `vehicles?`) with voxel indices in **that dimension's** coordinate space. `dimensionSectionOf(save, dimension)` maps the overworld to the top level and other dimensions to their section, so restore code is dimension-agnostic. An engine re-emits sections it does not simulate **verbatim** (`foreignDimensions` / `foreignOverworld` on `GameEngine`) — the server room (always overworld) round-trips a world's nether builds without knowing they exist. ⚠️ **Drift trap:** a field added to `serialize()`'s world half must be added to `DimensionSection` too, or it silently stays overworld-global (pinned by the byte-equality pass-through test in `GameEngine.test.ts`)
55:- **v18** (dimensions — the nether) — adds optional top-level `worldgenVersion` and `dimensions`, and optional per-player `dimension`/`portalArrival` (all described above). `migrateSaveV17toV18` is a **pure version bump**: no data moves — the top-level world fields remain the overworld's, so every pre-v18 save loads as an overworld-only world with the guard grandfathered (no stamp ⇒ never fires). The nether's own generator (`lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`) is a separate byte contract with its own SHA-256 baselines; adding it changed **no overworld bytes**, so `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays **11** — but from here on a bump discards **both** dimensions' diffs together (one stamp governs the whole save). The `NetherPortal` `BlockId` (91) is appended and has no item; `Obsidian` (90) and the new items (buckets, flint & steel) are additive string ids.
56:- **v17** (the players array — multiplayer groundwork) — every per-player field moves off the top level into `players: SavedPlayer[]`; world-level fields (seed, worldType, difficulty, hardcore, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, villagesSeeded) stay put. `SavedPlayer` keeps the old field names (one rename: the top-level `player` position becomes `position`) so the per-field validators are shared between migration and live restores. `migrateSaveV16toV17` is a pure field move wrapping a flat single-player save as `[{ id: "local", … }]`, and rewrites pet owners from the legacy literal `"player"` to `"local"` — `SavedMob.owner` is a real player id from here on. A single-player world always saves one `"local"` entry; a multiplayer server holds one entry per known account and restores a joining player's slice through the same `restorePlayerFields` mirror that `serialize()` writes. Hardcore's `gameOver` is per-player (`restoreGameOver(save, savedPlayer)` requires the world's `hardcore` flag as before).
57:- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11)** — **portable worldgen noise**. Every seed-determined noise call (terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, the underground speckle hash) moved from `Math.sin` — whose results are engine-defined, so the same seed could generate different terrain on different JS engines — to the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts`. Same formulas, near-identical terrain (all structural probes unchanged), but exact bytes shift: old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed, and all worldgen digests were re-baselined into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` per docs/testing.md. The save **schema stays v16** — no field changes. This makes seed + block-diff sync portable between a browser and a Bun multiplayer server, and is proven in CI by `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` (Chromium digest ≡ Bun baseline). Weather windows and the daylight curve moved to the same portable primitives (both transient/derived — no save impact).
58:- **0.12.0 (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
59:- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
60:- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
61:- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
62:- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
63:- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
64:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
65:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
66:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

lines: - `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed

- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it

- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations

-- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of **worldgen** loot chests (dungeon, shipwreck, or buried treasure) the player has already opened or broken. Worldgen chests' contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`, mixed with a per-family constant, from the family's own table) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only sets of _which_ indices belong to each family are not stored; they are re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` / `collectShipwreckSites` / `collectTreasureSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). The field kept its name when shipwrecks/buried treasure generalized it (state-side it is `lootedWorldgenChests`), so pre-aquatic saves read unchanged. Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

- `stats` (optional) — gameplay **statistics** as `{ id, value }[]` (blocks mined, mobs killed, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, distance travelled, time played, …). Counters live in `state.stats` (a `Map<string, number>`) and are folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint (`recordEvent`/`recordTick`, `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`). Like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, they are a long-term record and are **kept across death**. Only positive values are written; `restoreStats` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops non-string ids and negative/garbage values. The id set is open (per-recipe `crafted_<id>` and per-block `*_mined` counters), so there's no allow-list

- `advancements` (optional) — the unlocked **advancement** ids as `string[]`. Unlock is uniform — `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold` for each declarative entry in `ADVANCEMENTS` (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`) — and ids accumulate in `state.advancements` (a `Set`). Also **kept across death**; `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) keeps non-empty strings only, de-duplicated. Unknown persisted ids (e.g. a renamed entry) are harmless: they round-trip but never re-unlock, since `evaluateAdvancements` only iterates the registry

- `mobs` (optional) — persisted mobs as `SavedMob[]` (`{ kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer?, profession? }`). The fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot by `spawnInitialMobs`, so only mobs matching `isPersistentMob` are written: **tamed pets** (`owner` set) and **village residents** (`faction === "villager"`). `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate — dropping unknown kinds, non-finite coords, non-positive hp, and anything that isn't a valid persistent shape (an owned ally pet, or an owner-less villager); a resident's `profession` (v15) is validated against the known set. The engine rebuilds each live `MobState` **before** `spawnInitialMobs`, re-grounding `y` onto the current surface (the world may have changed), assigning fresh ids (the renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot), and clamping hp + re-arming a pet's detect range. Like `xp`/`stats` and **unlike `effects`**, persisted mobs are kept across death

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Nether fortresses & deep redstone ore — the worldgen v12 batch (save v18 and protocol v4 unchanged; ⚠ existing worlds discard their block edits in BOTH dimensions and reboot from seed)**: the Nether gets a destination and redstone-lite gets its real ore, bundled into one `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump so players' edits are discarded once, not twice. **Fortresses** rise over the lava seas — an 11×11 nether-brick keep with four covered, railed bridges striding out to 7×7 watchtowers, glowstone lamps in the ceilings and windowed walls — holding the dimension's first **loot chests** (lazily filled on first open from their own table, riding the existing persisted `lootedChests` machinery: nether-brick salvage always, glowstone dust/gold/coal/bread/redstone dust often, and a rare tier of blazite ore, **obsidian** — a portal-repair kit — diamond ore, or a sapphire sword) and usually a **spawner** dripping imps and the odd scorcher under the same rules as dungeon spawners. Looting your first fortress chest unlocks the **Fortress Raider** advancement, and a **Fortress Chests Looted** statistic counts on. Placement is PRNG-pure (the carved nether has no seed-pure surface to validate against), which is what lets the engine — client, server shard, or replica — re-derive every chest and spawner cell from the seed alone; separation guarantees two fortresses can never touch. The fortress material is yours to keep: **nether brick** smelts from netherrack 1:1 (no fuel), and crafts **slabs and stairs** at the family ratios — a second partial-block id range behind the same predicates, so auto step-up, mob grounding, and the floor-fitting refusal all just apply. Meanwhile the overworld's deeps (Y ≤ 24) now vein **redstone ore**: sliver-pickaxe-gated, each block shattering into 4–5 **redstone dust** plus Fortune's level — and the gold+coal dust recipe from redstone-lite's launch is **retired** (it was an explicit stopgap for exactly this batch; the recipe-book hint now reads "Mine redstone ore"). The ore pass runs last and replaces stone only, so it can neither shift another generation stream nor eat a dungeon's cobble walls; all eleven worldgen digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md, with every structural probe passing unchanged.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Nether fortresses & deep redstone ore — the worldgen v12 batch (save v18 and protocol v4 unchanged; ⚠ existing worlds discard their block edits in BOTH dimensions and reboot from seed)**: the Nether gets a destination and redstone-lite gets its real ore, bundled into one `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump so players' edits are discarded once, not twice. **Fortresses** rise over the lava seas — an 11×11 nether-brick keep with four covered, railed bridges striding out to 7×7 watchtowers, glowstone lamps in the ceilings and windowed walls — holding the dimension's first **loot chests** (lazily filled on first open from their own table, riding the existing persisted `lootedChests` machinery: nether-brick salvage always, glowstone dust/gold/coal/bread/redstone dust often, and a rare tier of blazite ore, **obsidian** — a portal-repair kit — diamond ore, or a sapphire sword) and usually a **spawner** dripping imps and the odd scorcher under the same rules as dungeon spawners. Looting your first fortress chest unlocks the **Fortress Raider** advancement, with a **Fortress Chests Looted** statistic counting on. Placement is PRNG-pure (the carved nether has no seed-pure surface to validate against), which is what lets any engine — client, server shard, or replica — re-derive every chest and spawner cell from the seed alone; a separation floor guarantees two fortresses can never touch. The fortress material is yours to keep: **nether brick** smelts from netherrack 1:1 (no fuel) and crafts **slabs and stairs** at the family ratios — a second partial-block id range behind the same predicates, so auto step-up, mob grounding, and the floor-fitting refusal all just apply. Meanwhile the overworld's deeps (Y ≤ 24) now vein **redstone ore**: sliver-pickaxe-gated, each block shattering into 4–5 **redstone dust** plus Fortune's level — and the gold+coal dust recipe from redstone-lite's launch is **retired** (it was an explicit stopgap for exactly this batch; the recipe-book hint now reads "Mine redstone ore"). The ore pass runs last and replaces stone only, so it can neither shift another generation stream nor eat a dungeon's cobble walls; all eleven worldgen digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md, with every structural probe passing unchanged.

docs/architecture.md:82:**Dungeon loot chests.** Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents can't ride the block-diff baseline. The engine instead keeps two session-only sets — `dungeonChestIndices` / `dungeonSpawnerIndices` — rebuilt each boot from the seed via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`, which replays the dungeon placement math without writing blocks), plus a **persisted** `lootedDungeonChests` set. On a dungeon chest's first open or break, `systems/dungeon.ts` `fillDungeonChestIfUnlooted` rolls loot seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex` (`lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`) and marks the index looted. Gating on the looted set — not on whether the chest is currently non-empty — is what stops an emptied-then-reloaded chest from re-rolling (an empty container is dropped from `blockEntities`).
docs/architecture.md:152:- `generation.ts` — `generateWorld(world)`: deterministic terrain, caves, lava, water, ores, trees, houses, and underground dungeons (`placeDungeons`, last in the pipeline). `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` (so it can't shift ore RNG) and before `placeDungeons` (so rooms overwrite lava). `collectDungeonSites(world)` re-derives dungeon chest/spawner indices from the seed for the engine. Constants live in the frozen `GEN` object. **Byte-identical output per seed is a save-format contract**, pinned by `generation.test.ts` hash tests — fix code, never hashes.
docs/adding-content.md:89:- A hypothetical third dimension would extend: `DimensionId` (types.ts — the compile-enforced `VALID_DIMENSIONS` and `DIMENSION_PROFILES` records then demand entries), `SaveData.dimensions`, `dimensionSectionOf`, its own generator module with pinned SHA-256 baselines (the `netherGeneration.ts` pattern: portable noise, fresh PRNG xor constants, area-scaled counts), and each seam above.
docs/adding-content.md:125:- If the structure needs its positions known at runtime (dungeons re-derive chest/spawner indices on load, **villages** re-derive their centers to seed residents), expose a **derive pass** like `collectDungeonSites`/`collectVillageSites`: factor placement into a shared routine that either writes blocks or records indices, drawing from a **dedicated PRNG seeded only from `world.seed`** (`villageRand`) with a fixed number of draws per structure, and validate against **seed-pure** terrain (`terrainTopY`, `getBiome`) — never `highestSolidY`, which a cave or player edit can shift out from under the derive pass.

## A worldgen structure (houses, dungeons, …)

- Structures are placed in `lib/world/generation.ts` at the end of the `generateWorld` pipeline. Mirror `placeHouse`/`placeDungeons`: loop a `GEN.<thing>Count`, sample positions, validate, and write blocks with `world.set`. Append your pass **last** so later passes don't overwrite it, and add the count to the frozen `GEN` object.
- **Any block write changes the deterministic output**, so this breaks the worldgen hash. Re-baseline the `generation.test.ts` digests and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` per the [testing.md](testing.md) policy (each world then discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed); add a structural probe test (count your blocks, assert they generate) that survives the re-baseline.
- If the structure needs its positions known at runtime (dungeons re-derive chest/spawner indices on load, **villages** re-derive their centers to seed residents), expose a **derive pass** like `collectDungeonSites`/`collectVillageSites`: factor placement into a shared routine that either writes blocks or records indices, drawing from a **dedicated PRNG seeded only from `world.seed`** (`villageRand`) with a fixed number of draws per structure, and validate against **seed-pure** terrain (`terrainTopY`, `getBiome`) — never `highestSolidY`, which a cave or player edit can shift out from under the derive pass.
- **Shipwrecks and buried treasure** are the worked examples of chest-bearing structures: each runs on its own decoupled PRNG (fresh xor constant — coal and villages already collide on one), draws a **fixed number of randoms per attempt** whether or not it places, and validates seed-purely (`getBiome` + `terrainTopY` bands; buried treasure's "beach" is a terrain-height proxy, never `placeBeaches`' block reads). Their `collect*Sites` derives feed the generalized worldgen-chest fill (below) and, for treasure, the map compass.
- **Villages** are the worked example of a structure that spawns mobs: `placeVillages` levels a small terrace and builds via the shared `buildHouseShell`, the engine seeds resident villagers at each `collectVillageSites` center, and those residents **persist** (they're `faction === "villager"`, so `isPersistentMob` keeps them) — so a structure's mobs only spawn when the world has none yet (a fresh world or a worldgen-upgrade), never on every reload.

## A loot table / lazy block-entity fill

- Drop tables are pure data + a roll function: copy the `{ itemId, min, max, chance? }` shape and the `clampUnit` roll loop from `lib/game/mobLoot.ts` / `lib/game/dungeonLoot.ts`. Add a `*.test.ts` asserting every `itemId` exists in `ITEM_DEFS` and that rolls are deterministic under an injected rng.
- To fill a **worldgen-placed** block-entity (a dungeon, shipwreck, or buried-treasure chest) whose contents can't live in the block-diff baseline: fill it lazily on first access, seeded from `world.seed ^ voxelIndex ^ <family constant>` (`dungeonLoot.seededRng`), and persist a set of _accessed_ indices — gate the fill on that set, **not** on whether the container is currently non-empty, or an emptied-then-reloaded entity re-rolls. `lib/game/engine/systems/dungeon.ts` (`fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`), shared by the open and break paths, is the reference: the session-derived site set holding the index picks **both** the loot table and the seed family, and every family shares the one persisted `lootedChests` save field — so a new chest family needs a site derive + a table + a branch there, and **no save bump**. First-access side effects (the buried chest's `treasureUnearthed` event) hook in the same place. See the exploit-guard tests in `GameEngine.test.ts`. Share the tier machinery via `rollTieredLoot` (`dungeonLoot.ts`) rather than copying the roll loop.

## A status effect (timed buff / hazard)

- Effects live in `state.effects: Map<EffectId, number>` (id → remaining seconds), driven by `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts`. Add an id to the `EffectId` union (`lib/game/types.ts`) and to `EFFECT_ORDER` + the `clearEffects`/helper logic; durations/strengths go in `config.ts`.
- **Apply it at one seam.** Each existing effect reads at exactly one place: Speed multiplies `playerMotion.ts` speed (`speedMultiplier`), Strength adds to the melee dispatch in `GameEngine.ts` (`strengthBonus`), Fire Resistance / Water Breathing are booleans passed into `tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen` (`playerStats.ts`), and Regeneration/Poison run inside `tickStatusEffects` on their **own** accumulators. Prefer a gate/modifier over a new tick; `tickStatusEffects` already runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks, so its gates are current.
- **Damage that shouldn't kill** uses `applyNonLethalDamage` (`playerLife.ts`), not `applyUnmitigatedDamage` — poison floors at `POISON_FLOOR_HP`.
- **Grant it.** A drinkable potion is a `material` item with an `effect: { id, durationSeconds }` (`ItemDef`/`InventorySlot`); the `drinkPotion` command and the `F` key apply it via `addEffect`. A brewed potion is a `station: "brewing"` recipe (see "A new item or recipe"). A hazard source just calls `addEffect` (e.g. the rotten-flesh roll in the `eatFood` case, using the injected `this.rng`).
- **Show it.** Add a `HudIconName` + grid in `hudPixels.ts`; the cached `effectsProjection` in `GameEngine` feeds `GameSnapshot.activeEffects`, which `ActiveEffects.tsx` renders — keep the projection ref-stable (rebuild only when rounded seconds change) so the HUD doesn't thrash.
---

## A status effect (timed buff / hazard)

- Effects live in `state.effects: Map<EffectId, number>` (id → remaining seconds), driven by `lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts`. Add an id to the `EffectId` union (`lib/game/types.ts`) and to `EFFECT_ORDER` + the `clearEffects`/helper logic; durations/strengths go in `config.ts`.
- **Apply it at one seam.** Each existing effect reads at exactly one place: Speed multiplies `playerMotion.ts` speed (`speedMultiplier`), Strength adds to the melee dispatch in `GameEngine.ts` (`strengthBonus`), Fire Resistance / Water Breathing are booleans passed into `tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen` (`playerStats.ts`), and Regeneration/Poison run inside `tickStatusEffects` on their **own** accumulators. Prefer a gate/modifier over a new tick; `tickStatusEffects` already runs after `tickHealthRegen` and before the environmental ticks, so its gates are current.
- **Damage that shouldn't kill** uses `applyNonLethalDamage` (`playerLife.ts`), not `applyUnmitigatedDamage` — poison floors at `POISON_FLOOR_HP`.
- **Grant it.** A drinkable potion is a `material` item with an `effect: { id, durationSeconds }` (`ItemDef`/`InventorySlot`); the `drinkPotion` command and the `F` key apply it via `addEffect`. A brewed potion is a `station: "brewing"` recipe (see "A new item or recipe"). A hazard source just calls `addEffect` (e.g. the rotten-flesh roll in the `eatFood` case, using the injected `this.rng`).
- **Show it.** Add a `HudIconName` + grid in `hudPixels.ts`; the cached `effectsProjection` in `GameEngine` feeds `GameSnapshot.activeEffects`, which `ActiveEffects.tsx` renders — keep the projection ref-stable (rebuild only when rounded seconds change) so the HUD doesn't thrash.

1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47	
48	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
49	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
50	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.
51	
52	| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
53	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
55	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
56	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
57	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
58	
59	## Recipes
60	
61	**100 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
62	All use the always-available crafting grid except the **furnace** smelting recipes
63	(need an open furnace) and the eight **brewing** recipes (need an open
64	[brewing stand](#brewing--potions)). The tables below show 92 rows: each furnace
65	"+ Fuel" row (and the torch) collapses its separate coal and charcoal recipes
66	into one line.
67	
68	In-game, the recipe book groups recipes into the sections below (Tools, Vehicles,
69	Weapons, Armor, Building, Food, Materials, then Smelting, Brewing, and Trades), listing the

## What got built

**Nether fortresses** — an 11×11 nether-brick keep with four covered bridges spanning the lava seas, each ending in a 7×7 watchtower, with glowstone lamps and windowed walls. The keep holds the dimension's first loot chests (a new family on the existing `lootedChests` machinery — no save bump) plus a spawner dripping imps/scorchers; most towers hold a chest. First loot unlocks the **Fortress Raider** advancement, with a **Fortress Chests Looted** statistic alongside. **Redstone ore** now veins the deep overworld (Y ≤ 24, sliver-pickaxe-gated), the gold+coal dust recipe is retired, and **nether brick** smelts from netherrack and crafts slabs/stairs. All under one WORLDGEN_VERSION 11→12 bump; save v18 and protocol v4 untouched, and online play needed zero wire changes.

## Verification

Full gate green: lint (only the 2 pre-existing GameShell warnings), typecheck, format, build, 1494 unit tests, and **all 35 local Playwright e2e** — including the Chromium determinism spec recomputing the full-world digest against the 11 re-baselined hashes. Port 3000 was held by your astra dev server, so e2e ran via the alt-port trick (temporary config edit, reverted). One unit test timed out in the load-heavy run right after e2e (`server/room.test.ts` speed-hack pose, a 5s timeout); it passed 2/2 in isolation and in three earlier full runs — the known kind of load flake.

## Deviations from the approved plan, with reasons

- **Redstone ore drops 4–5 dust per block** (glowstone-style multi-drop, Fortune adds its level) instead of the planned 1-per-block — retiring an 8-dust recipe meant one vein must fund a real circuit.
- **No spawn-distance gate on fortresses** — portals exit at their overworld coordinates, so there's no "nether spawn" cell to protect; separation went 64→**72** so two fortresses' longest opposing arms (2×35=70) can mathematically never overwrite each other's chests.
- The meshing digest **didn't** need re-baselining after all — ore swaps one solid cube for another, so vertex positions are byte-identical.
- Small bonuses: typecheck caught the exhaustive audio-materials table for the new blocks, and the docs pass fixed pre-existing drift (stale pre-aquatic names in architecture.md, missing stat rows, a recipe count stuck at 74).

**What's left for you:** the usual manual gameplay pass before this merges — portal in, find a fortress, walk a bridge, loot a chest (toast + chime), watch the spawner, mine redstone ore, place the new slabs/stairs, and confirm the recipe book hints "Mine redstone ore". content.text:
Now that the fortress batch is merged, here's my updated ranking — all grounded in this session's exploration:

**1. The deferred combat & magic batch (my top pick).** The list that's been deferred since v0.11.0: **Fire Aspect** (needs a small per-mob burn timer — mobs have no status machinery, but the kill-credit plumbing already anticipates indirect "burn" kills), **Thorns** (thread the attacker through `damagePlayer`, which today passes a bare amount), **Night Vision** (a renderer brightness seam — currently global, driven only by daylight), **Invisibility** (nearly free: one check in `nearestTargetablePlayer`, the single aggro chokepoint every hunting mob uses), and **splash potions** (a third thrown system modeled on spears, with the explosion system's radial scan applying `addEffect` instead of damage). It's the right contrast after two worldgen-heavy epics: pure mechanics depth, **no worldgen bump, no save bump** (new enchant/effect ids ride the existing validated fields), each piece severable. High value per effort.

**2. Horses & land mounts.** Fun and highly visible, but honest sizing: no rideable-mob machinery exists — vehicles are hard-gated to water/rail and `MobState` has no rider field. The mounted-player multiplayer model from boats would transfer, but taming + ground movement + mount plumbing is a real epic.

**3. Pistons (instant-push).** Extends redstone-lite with block-motion — feasible within the id-swap model (shift a line of blocks one cell on a power edge, no animation). Great for the circuit-builder loop that redstone + rails + the new ore now feed.

**4. The End-style finale dimension.** The Dragon Lord fight currently happens in the overworld; moving it to a third dimension is much cheaper post-Nether, but the server's shard lifecycle is still hardcoded to `nether` (`dormantNether`/`sweepNetherShard`/`composeSave`), and `DimensionId` is a closed two-value union — so it starts with a generalization pass. Worth doing eventually, not next.

Hoppers/item automation stay blocked — drops go straight to inventory, no ground-item entity exists.

**Before any of these, though, two pieces of housekeeping:** the merged batch still isn't on prod — e2e re-run attempt 3 is in flight (two different multiplayer specs flaked across attempts; deploys held until green) — and the **manual gameplay passes are piling up** (this batch's fortress/ore/slabs pass, plus several older ones). Once the deploy lands and the manual pass is done, cutting **v0.17.0** would bundle the Nether-online + fortress work into a release before starting the next epic.

If you want to proceed, I'd say: let me confirm the deploy goes green, then start the combat & magic batch.
