content.text:
Yes — attempt 3 failed on the **same spec again**: `nether-online.e2e.ts`, the two-player portal journey. Here's what I've established:

**What's failing.** Always the same step — the host building the obsidian portal frame in the *overworld* (`placeAt`, line 289). Attempt 3 gave a concrete error: `could not place block 90 at (271,47,252)` — the server never confirmed a frame block, through both aim retries.

**Why I'm confident it's not the fortress batch.** The failing step happens before any nether interaction; obsidian placement touches none of the new code branches (it's not a stair/overlay/rail, so the new predicates never fire); the overworld surface at the build height is byte-identical pre/post batch (redstone ore only replaces stone at Y ≤ 24); and the spec **passed attempt 1 on this very merge commit**, plus twice locally. The scoreboard across identical code: attempt 1 — friend-dig failed, portal journey passed; attempts 2–3 — friend-dig passed, portal journey failed. Two different heavyweight multiplayer specs trading places is runner-environment behavior, not a regression.

**Likely mechanism.** The server re-raycasts each `placeBlock` from *its* view of the placer's pose. On the loaded CI runner (two Chromiums + Next + the game server on one box), the pose stream lags the scripted aim, the server's ray lands on the wrong cell, and the spec's retry budget is thin — 2 aim candidates, one 150 ms settle, 8 s witness poll. This spec is the heaviest in the suite by its own header comment (~15 server-confirmed placements, two signups, two nether worldgens).

**Where things stand.** Attempt 4 is running now. If it goes green, the deploys fire and we're done. If it reds again, I'd stop the re-run roulette — the honest fix is a dedicated deflake session for this spec (fatten the aim/retry budget, or drive placement confirmation off the server echo per block, following the same playbook that fixed the touch flakes). I've written the full diagnosis into the project notes either way. Note there's no prod urgency: main is save-compatible and protocol-unchanged, so nothing live is stale while the gate holds.

content.text:
To answer your question directly: the first two re-runs were justified — the evidence then pointed at random runner load (two *different* specs failing on identical code, each passing in the other attempt), and you don't rewrite a test on one bad sample. But you're right that by the third same-spec failure it stopped being noise and became a pattern that deserved a fix, so that's what I've done:

**Root cause.** The spec aims by writing yaw/pitch into local state, sleeps a blind 150 ms, then dispatches `placeBlock`. The server re-raycasts from **its** copy of the player's pose, fed by the 20 Hz pose stream — and on a loaded CI runner that stream can lag the scripted aim by whole seconds, so the server raycasts with a stale look direction and the block lands (or fails) on the wrong cell. Two aim candidates × one blind sleep = a thin budget that CI kept blowing through.

**The fix** (in `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts`): a new `poseSettled` gate — before every dispatch, poll until the *witness browser* sees the placer at the intended pose. That's proof the aim round-tripped placer → server → witness, so the server's raycast provably runs from the right pose; no more guessing with sleeps. The candidate loop also gets three rounds instead of one, the ignition dispatch gets the same gate, and the failure message now dumps the placer's pose/held-item/net-state so any future failure is diagnosable instead of mute.

**Validation plan.** Running the spec twice locally now (in progress). But per this repo's own hard-learned lesson, local green is *not* sufficient for CI flakes — the only true validation is main's CI. So once local passes I'll commit straight to main (test-only fix) and push, which triggers a fresh gated run. Attempt 4 of the old run is still in flight and won't be canceled by the push — whichever goes green first releases the deploys.

Second-round fix is in, validating locally now (both two-browser specs this time, since the throttling mechanism implicates friend-dig too). What changed beyond round one:

1. **Root cause, config level**: Chromium launch args disabling background-tab throttling (`--disable-background-timer-throttling`, `--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows`, `--disable-renderer-backgrounding`). The spec's `host.bringToFront()` backgrounds the friend page for the whole build phase, and a throttled friend stops applying server ticks — which starves every witness-side assertion. This also covers the historic friend-dig flake, which uses the same two-context pattern.
2. **Structural, spec level**: `placeAt` no longer depends solely on the witness — fast witness confirmation first, then a placer-side fallback: a block still standing 5.5 s after dispatch has outlived the prediction-revert window (`PREDICTION_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS` = 5 s), so it's provably server-confirmed even if the witness page is being starved. Ignition's existing two-page portal poll keeps the end-to-end replication guarantee honest.
3. Budget hygiene: settle poll capped at 5 s, test timeout 360 → 480 s.

Once local passes, I'll commit and push; CI validates for real.

content.content:
e2e:
    # Browser e2e takes several times longer than verify, so it gates merges
    # to main (the push event), not every PR iteration — PRs still run the
    # full verify job, and renderer/input/shell work runs e2e locally per
    # AGENTS.md before landing.
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

input.prompt:
Audit the Playwright e2e suite in /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/e2e/ (10 files: accountSp, cloudSaves, determinism, menu, multiplayer, nether-online, portal, pwa, smoke, touch — plus helpers.ts and onlineHelpers.ts) for PARALLEL-SAFETY. Today the suite runs with workers:1 against ONE shared Next server (pglite://memory Postgres) and ONE shared Bun game server (PERSISTENCE=memory). I want to run specs from DIFFERENT FILES concurrently (workers:2, fullyParallel stays false so tests within a file stay serial). Search breadth: medium.

Answer precisely with file paths:
1. Account/email collisions: which specs sign up online accounts, and how do they generate emails/usernames? (e.g. runTag = Date.now().toString(36)) — could two specs starting in the same millisecond collide? Are the email prefixes distinct per spec file?
2. Game-server room usage: which specs create ONLINE (server-backed) worlds — i.e., consume game-server rooms? The e2e game server has some MAX_ROOMS (check server config/env — server/index.ts or room manager) — what's the cap, and could 2 concurrent multiplayer-ish specs exceed it? Do rooms get evicted/freed when a spec's pages close?
3. Shared-state hazards: any spec that mutates GLOBAL state on the shared servers — e.g., assumes it's the only world in /api/worlds responses (like nether-online's worlds[0].id — is that scoped to the signed-in account or global?), relies on being the only connected socket, asserts on server-wide counts, or manipulates the system clock?
4. Browser-context isolation: specs using localStorage/IndexedDB (single-player worlds) — are they per browser context (fresh context per test) so concurrent specs can't see each other's storage? Does the pwa spec's offline mode or service worker cut affect only its own context?
5. Any test.describe.configure / serial-mode / ordering dependencies BETWEEN files (spec A assumes spec B ran first)?
6. Anything else that breaks with 2 workers: fixed ports besides the shared servers, singleton lock files, screenshot/name collisions, the helpers' gamePage fixture using global state?

Return a compact verdict per file: SAFE / RISKY (why) for concurrent execution with one other file.

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here is the audit.

## Environment facts (confirmed)

- `playwright.config.ts:44-72` — ONE shared Next server (`DATABASE_URL: pglite://memory`, port 3000) and ONE shared Bun game server (`PERSISTENCE: memory`, port 18080). The game server env sets only `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` — it does **not** set `MAX_ROOMS`, so the cap is the default **6** (`server/index.ts:25`).
- Room lifecycle (`server/roomRegistry.ts`): rooms are keyed by `worldId`; a room is created on first join and evicted only after `IDLE_EVICT_MS = 5 min` of being empty, swept every 30s (`roomRegistry.ts:13,26-27,61-68`). The join cap is enforced at `roomRegistry.ts:38` (`rooms.size + loading.size >= maxRooms` → refuse). Nether is an internal shard of the SAME `Room` object (`roomRegistry.ts:6-10`), so a nether trip does **not** consume a second registry slot.
- `/api/worlds` GET is **account-scoped**: `route.ts:7-11` → `listWorlds(db, user.id)` filters by `worldMembers.userId = userId` (`lib/online/worldsService.ts:145-150`). So `worlds[0].id` returns only the signed-in account's worlds, not a global list.
- No `test.describe.configure`, no `serial` mode, no `test.slow`, no hardcoded ports, no `/health` or `/rooms` or diagnostics calls anywhere in `e2e/` (grep clean).

## 1. Account/email collisions

Specs that sign up online accounts and their email prefixes:
- `e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts:41` — `roamer-${Date.now().toString(36)}@example.com`
- `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts:54` — `cloudy-${Date.now().toString(36)}@example.com`
- `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts:47,58,92` — `host-${runTag}@…`, `friend-${runTag}@…`
- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts:224,231,256` — `portal-host-${runTag}@…`, `portal-friend-${runTag}@…`

Every prefix is **distinct per file**. Two files starting in the same millisecond produce the same `runTag` but different prefixes, so the emails never collide. The only global uniqueness constraint is the email (better-auth on the shared pglite DB); display/profile names are account-scoped so their reuse is harmless. **No collision risk across files.** (Same-file retries recompute `Date.now()` and run serially, so no intra-file risk either.)

## 2. Game-server room usage

Only two files create ONLINE (server-backed) worlds:
- `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — 1 online world (host creates, friend joins the same room) = 1 room.
- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` — 1 online world = 1 room (the nether shard is inside that same room, not a second slot).

`accountSp.e2e.ts:71` and `cloudSaves.e2e.ts` create **sp-cloud** worlds and explicitly assert `net == null` — they use the `/api/worlds` blob API only and **never touch the game server**, so they consume zero rooms.

Cap: default **6**. With `workers:2`, the maximum concurrent room-consuming pair is multiplayer + nether-online = **2 live rooms ≤ 6**. Comfortable headroom. Rooms are freed lazily: closing the contexts (`multiplayer.e2e.ts:198-199`, `nether-online.e2e.ts:438-439`) fires the socket `close` → `room.leave` → `playerCount → 0`, but the room object lingers up to 5 min before the sweeper evicts it. That doesn't matter for concurrency because each spec run creates a **fresh** `worldId` → a **fresh** room slot; the only accumulation risk is CI retries (`retries:3`) piling idle-but-unswept rooms, but with just two room-creating files running serially on their own workers this stays well under 6. **Safe, but this is the one axis to watch if more online spec files are ever added.**

## 3. Shared-state hazards

- `worlds[0].id` in `multiplayer.e2e.ts:74` and `nether-online.e2e.ts:245` — account-scoped (see above). Each host is a brand-new account with exactly one world, so `[0]` is correct regardless of ordering or concurrency. **Not global.**
- `players.size === 2` / roster assertions (`multiplayer.e2e.ts:106,133`, `nether-online.e2e.ts:263,391,409`) are scoped to that spec's own room. Distinct worldIds ⇒ no cross-talk. **Safe.**
- No spec asserts on server-wide counts (no `/health`, `/rooms`, or diagnostics reads).
- No system-clock manipulation. `Date.now()` is used only for email tags. `net.setSimulatedLatency` (`multiplayer.e2e.ts:162,183`) is per client session, not global.

## 4. Browser-context isolation

All single-player specs (`smoke`, `touch`, `determinism`, `portal` via the `gamePage` fixture in `helpers.ts:26`; `menu` and `cloudSaves`/`accountSp` via raw `page`/`browser.newContext()`) run in the default **per-test browser context**, which Playwright fully partitions. localStorage keys (`minecraft_profiles_v1`, `minecraft_worlds_v1`, etc.) and the IndexedDB `monecraft` DB (`helpers.ts:143`) are per-context, so concurrent specs cannot see each other's storage even though the fixture reuses the fixed ids `e2e-profile`/`e2e-world`. **Safe.**

`pwa.e2e.ts` — `context.setOffline(true)` (line 77) and the service-worker registration/precache are **per browser context**; each Playwright worker also has its own browser. The offline cut and SW only affect the pwa test's own context, not other files. (The header comment even notes all suites now run with the SW registering by design.) **Safe.**

## 5. Ordering dependencies between files

None. No `test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" })`, no cross-file assumptions, no reliance on file execution order. Each file is self-contained (registers its own account or seeds its own storage). **Safe.**

## 6. Anything else that breaks with 2 workers

- Fixed ports: only 3000 and 18080, both the shared servers. No spec binds its own port. **Safe.**
- Lock files / singletons: `pglite://memory` is in-process to the Next server; game server is `PERSISTENCE=memory`. No files, no locks. **Safe.**
- Screenshots/traces: `trace: retain-on-failure` only; Playwright namespaces artifacts by test title + worker, and all titles are unique across files. **Safe.**
- `gamePage` fixture (`helpers.ts:9-88`): uses `addInitScript` + `page` (per-context) state and the per-page `window.__monecraft` handle — no process-global state. **Safe.**

---

## Per-file verdict (concurrent with one other file)

- `e2e/accountSp.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Fresh contexts, unique `roamer-` email, sp-cloud (no room), account-scoped `/api/worlds`.
- `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Own context, unique `cloudy-` email, sp-cloud (no room), account-scoped world lookup.
- `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Pure local worldgen digest in an isolated context; no server or shared state.
- `e2e/menu.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Local-only menus, per-test context storage, no online/server touch.
- `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Consumes 1 room; unique `host-`/`friend-` emails; all assertions room-scoped. (Room-consuming — counts toward the cap-of-6 headroom, but only 2 such files exist.)
- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Consumes 1 room (nether shard is internal); unique `portal-host-`/`portal-friend-` emails; `worlds[0].id` account-scoped; room-scoped `players.size`.
- `e2e/portal.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Single-player via `gamePage`, no `net`, isolated context.
- `e2e/pwa.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Per-context service worker + `setOffline`; no cross-context leak; no rooms.
- `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Single-player fixture, per-context localStorage/IndexedDB, no server.
- `e2e/touch.e2e.ts` — **SAFE.** Single-player fixture on a phone viewport; isolated context; no server.

**Overall verdict: the suite is parallel-safe at `workers:2` with `fullyParallel:false`.** The only structural thing to keep an eye on is the shared game server's default `MAX_ROOMS=6` versus the number of online-world spec files (currently 2). If you add more online spec files, or want a safety margin against CI-retry room accumulation (5-min idle eviction), consider bumping the game server's `MAX_ROOMS` in `playwright.config.ts:66-71` — but nothing today requires it.

# E2E suite: fix the CPU-starvation flake and cut the runtime

## Context

The CI e2e suite takes 41–66 min (11 min locally) and has red-gated every deploy since the fortress batch merged. Two rounds of deflaking (`247a1c6` pose-settle, `702fcc2` no-throttle launch args + placer fallback) did not cure the portal-journey spec — the latest run still failed it 4/4 with the friend-dig spec flaking 3× beside it.

**Root-cause synthesis (from three failed runs' signatures):** the two-browser multiplayer specs run TWO full three.js render loops under software-GL (GitHub runners have no GPU) alongside the Next server and Bun game server on 4 vCPUs, with `retain-on-failure` tracing recording everything. The client's pose stream, command flushing, mining progress, and prediction reconciliation all ride the rAF loop — when software rasterization makes frames crawl, *everything* the specs assert on crawls: placements never confirm (portal journey), the friend's own digs never materialize (friend-dig line 177). It always passes on the Metal-GPU Mac; it coin-flips on CI; only the two-page specs fail. **Runtime and flakiness are the same problem: per-page CPU cost.**

User-chosen scope: config-level only (no CI-workflow sharding, no splitting the heavy spec), retries 3→2. Deploys have been held since v0.16.0 — this change is what unblocks them.

A parallel-safety audit (this session) cleared **all 10 spec files** for `workers: 2` with `fullyParallel: false`: distinct email prefixes per file, account-scoped `/api/worlds`, only 2 room-consuming files vs `MAX_ROOMS` default 6, per-context storage/service worker, no cross-file ordering.

## Changes

### A. Cut per-page CPU (the flake fix)

1. **Small viewports for the two-browser specs** — in `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` and `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`, create contexts with `viewport: { width: 640, height: 360 }` (~4× fewer pixels than the default 1280×720 → ~4× less software-GL raster work per page; these specs assert on `window.__monecraft` engine state, never pixels). The menu CSS already scrolls on small viewports (fixed in the game-modes era) and Playwright auto-scrolls targets. If any menu interaction breaks at 640×360 locally, fall back to 800×450.
2. **`trace: "retain-on-failure"` → `"on-first-retry"`** in `playwright.config.ts` — stops continuous trace recording on every first attempt (the 600–960 MB artifacts show its volume); retries still capture traces, which is when they're wanted.

### B. Parallelism + budget (the runtime fix)

3. **`workers: 2`** (CI and local) in `playwright.config.ts`; keep `fullyParallel: false` (file-level parallelism only, per the audit). With A1 in place, even the worst-case overlap (both heavy files concurrent = 4 game pages) is lighter than one heavy file today.
4. **`retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0`** (was 3) — caps a red run's tail.
5. **Reporter: add `"list"` on CI** (`[["github"], ["list"], ["html", …]]`) — the github reporter records no per-spec durations, which made this whole diagnosis harder than it needed to be.
6. **`MAX_ROOMS: "8"`** in the game-server `webServer` env — headroom against retry-accumulated idle rooms (5-min eviction) now that two room-consuming files can overlap.

### C. What NOT to touch

- No product code. No CI-workflow changes (`ci.yml` untouched). No changes to the deflake work from `247a1c6`/`702fcc2` — the pose-settle gate, placer fallback, and no-throttle args all remain (they're correct, just insufficient alone).
- Don't shrink the single-page specs' `gamePage` fixture viewport — those pass consistently; don't touch what works.

## Files

- `playwright.config.ts` — workers, retries, trace, reporter, MAX_ROOMS env.
- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts`, `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — context viewport at the two `browser.newContext()` sites in each.
- `docs/testing.md` — note the two-worker model, the viewport rationale, and the parallel-safety constraints (distinct email prefixes per file; room cap headroom) so future spec authors keep the invariants.

## Verification

1. **Local full suite** with the new config via the alt-port trick (port 3000 is held by another project; sed `playwright.config.ts` to 3100 + `PORT` env, **re-apply the intended config edits after any `git checkout` of that file** — a prior session lost uncommitted config edits that way). Expect ~5–7 min (from 11) and 35/35 green; watch the two heavy specs' menu flows at 640×360 specifically.
2. If green: commit straight to `main` (test-infra only, per repo convention), push, and watch the CI run — targets: **green e2e** and **≤ 25 min** wall (from 41–66). The run also releases the held `deploy-web`/`deploy-server` jobs for everything merged since v0.16.0.
3. If the heavy specs still red on CI with all of this in place, the next dials (follow-ups, not this change): pin the two heavy files to different workers or serial-only scheduling, CI-job sharding, or de-scoping the two-browser specs from the deploy gate to a nightly.
4. Record the outcome (either way) in the e2e-flakes memory note.

# E2E suite: fix the CPU-starvation flake and cut the runtime

## Context

The CI e2e suite takes 41–66 min (11 min locally) and has red-gated every deploy since the fortress batch merged. Two rounds of deflaking (`247a1c6` pose-settle, `702fcc2` no-throttle launch args + placer fallback) did not cure the portal-journey spec — the latest run still failed it 4/4 with the friend-dig spec flaking 3× beside it.

**Root-cause synthesis (from three failed runs' signatures):** the two-browser multiplayer specs run TWO full three.js render loops under software-GL (GitHub runners have no GPU) alongside the Next server and Bun game server on 4 vCPUs, with `retain-on-failure` tracing recording everything. The client's pose stream, command flushing, mining progress, and prediction reconciliation all ride the rAF loop — when software rasterization makes frames crawl, *everything* the specs assert on crawls: placements never confirm (portal journey), the friend's own digs never materialize (friend-dig line 177). It always passes on the Metal-GPU Mac; it coin-flips on CI; only the two-page specs fail. **Runtime and flakiness are the same problem: per-page CPU cost.**

User-chosen scope: config-level only (no CI-workflow sharding, no splitting the heavy spec), retries 3→2. Deploys have been held since v0.16.0 — this change is what unblocks them.

A parallel-safety audit (this session) cleared **all 10 spec files** for `workers: 2` with `fullyParallel: false`: distinct email prefixes per file, account-scoped `/api/worlds`, only 2 room-consuming files vs `MAX_ROOMS` default 6, per-context storage/service worker, no cross-file ordering.

## Changes

### A. Cut per-page CPU (the flake fix)

1. **Small viewports for the two-browser specs** — in `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` and `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`, create contexts with `viewport: { width: 640, height: 360 }` (~4× fewer pixels than the default 1280×720 → ~4× less software-GL raster work per page; these specs assert on `window.__monecraft` engine state, never pixels). The menu CSS already scrolls on small viewports (fixed in the game-modes era) and Playwright auto-scrolls targets. If any menu interaction breaks at 640×360 locally, fall back to 800×450.
2. **`trace: "retain-on-failure"` → `"on-first-retry"`** in `playwright.config.ts` — stops continuous trace recording on every first attempt (the 600–960 MB artifacts show its volume); retries still capture traces, which is when they're wanted.

### B. Parallelism + budget (the runtime fix)

3. **`workers: 2`** (CI and local) in `playwright.config.ts`; keep `fullyParallel: false` (file-level parallelism only, per the audit). With A1 in place, even the worst-case overlap (both heavy files concurrent = 4 game pages) is lighter than one heavy file today.
4. **`retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0`** (was 3) — caps a red run's tail.
5. **Reporter: add `"list"` on CI** (`[["github"], ["list"], ["html", …]]`) — the github reporter records no per-spec durations, which made this whole diagnosis harder than it needed to be.
6. **`MAX_ROOMS: "8"`** in the game-server `webServer` env — headroom against retry-accumulated idle rooms (5-min eviction) now that two room-consuming files can overlap.

### C. What NOT to touch

- No product code. No CI-workflow changes (`ci.yml` untouched). No changes to the deflake work from `247a1c6`/`702fcc2` — the pose-settle gate, placer fallback, and no-throttle args all remain (they're correct, just insufficient alone).
- Don't shrink the single-page specs' `gamePage` fixture viewport — those pass consistently; don't touch what works.

## Files

- `playwright.config.ts` — workers, retries, trace, reporter, MAX_ROOMS env.
- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts`, `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — context viewport at the two `browser.newContext()` sites in each.
- `docs/testing.md` — note the two-worker model, the viewport rationale, and the parallel-safety constraints (distinct email prefixes per file; room cap headroom) so future spec authors keep the invariants.

## Verification

1. **Local full suite** with the new config via the alt-port trick (port 3000 is held by another project; sed `playwright.config.ts` to 3100 + `PORT` env, **re-apply the intended config edits after any `git checkout` of that file** — a prior session lost uncommitted config edits that way). Expect ~5–7 min (from 11) and 35/35 green; watch the two heavy specs' menu flows at 640×360 specifically.
2. If green: commit straight to `main` (test-infra only, per repo convention), push, and watch the CI run — targets: **green e2e** and **≤ 25 min** wall (from 41–66). The run also releases the held `deploy-web`/`deploy-server` jobs for everything merged since v0.16.0.
3. If the heavy specs still red on CI with all of this in place, the next dials (follow-ups, not this change): pin the two heavy files to different workers or serial-only scheduling, CI-job sharding, or de-scoping the two-browser specs from the deploy gate to a nightly.
4. Record the outcome (either way) in the e2e-flakes memory note.

# E2E suite: fix the CPU-starvation flake and cut the runtime

## Context

The CI e2e suite takes 41–66 min (11 min locally) and has red-gated every deploy since the fortress batch merged. Two rounds of deflaking (`247a1c6` pose-settle, `702fcc2` no-throttle launch args + placer fallback) did not cure the portal-journey spec — the latest run still failed it 4/4 with the friend-dig spec flaking 3× beside it.

**Root-cause synthesis (from three failed runs' signatures):** the two-browser multiplayer specs run TWO full three.js render loops under software-GL (GitHub runners have no GPU) alongside the Next server and Bun game server on 4 vCPUs, with `retain-on-failure` tracing recording everything. The client's pose stream, command flushing, mining progress, and prediction reconciliation all ride the rAF loop — when software rasterization makes frames crawl, *everything* the specs assert on crawls: placements never confirm (portal journey), the friend's own digs never materialize (friend-dig line 177). It always passes on the Metal-GPU Mac; it coin-flips on CI; only the two-page specs fail. **Runtime and flakiness are the same problem: per-page CPU cost.**

User-chosen scope: config-level only (no CI-workflow sharding, no splitting the heavy spec), retries 3→2. Deploys have been held since v0.16.0 — this change is what unblocks them.

A parallel-safety audit (this session) cleared **all 10 spec files** for `workers: 2` with `fullyParallel: false`: distinct email prefixes per file, account-scoped `/api/worlds`, only 2 room-consuming files vs `MAX_ROOMS` default 6, per-context storage/service worker, no cross-file ordering.

## Changes

### A. Cut per-page CPU (the flake fix)

1. **Small viewports for the two-browser specs** — in `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts` and `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`, create contexts with `viewport: { width: 640, height: 360 }` (~4× fewer pixels than the default 1280×720 → ~4× less software-GL raster work per page; these specs assert on `window.__monecraft` engine state, never pixels). The menu CSS already scrolls on small viewports (fixed in the game-modes era) and Playwright auto-scrolls targets. If any menu interaction breaks at 640×360 locally, fall back to 800×450.
2. **`trace: "retain-on-failure"` → `"on-first-retry"`** in `playwright.config.ts` — stops continuous trace recording on every first attempt (the 600–960 MB artifacts show its volume); retries still capture traces, which is when they're wanted.

### B. Parallelism + budget (the runtime fix)

3. **`workers: 2`** (CI and local) in `playwright.config.ts`; keep `fullyParallel: false` (file-level parallelism only, per the audit). With A1 in place, even the worst-case overlap (both heavy files concurrent = 4 game pages) is lighter than one heavy file today.
4. **`retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0`** (was 3) — caps a red run's tail.
5. **Reporter: add `"list"` on CI** (`[["github"], ["list"], ["html", …]]`) — the github reporter records no per-spec durations, which made this whole diagnosis harder than it needed to be.
6. **`MAX_ROOMS: "8"`** in the game-server `webServer` env — headroom against retry-accumulated idle rooms (5-min eviction) now that two room-consuming files can overlap.

### C. What NOT to touch

- No product code. No CI-workflow changes (`ci.yml` untouched). No changes to the deflake work from `247a1c6`/`702fcc2` — the pose-settle gate, placer fallback, and no-throttle args all remain (they're correct, just insufficient alone).
- Don't shrink the single-page specs' `gamePage` fixture viewport — those pass consistently; don't touch what works.

- `e2e/nether-online.e2e.ts`, `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` — context viewport at the two `browser.newContext()` sites in each.

Browser-context storage (localStorage/IndexedDB/service worker) is Playwright-isolated per test, so concurrent files can't see each other's saves.

Three defenses are load-bearing: the quarter-size `TWO_BROWSER_VIEWPORT` (`onlineHelpers.ts` — raster cost scales with pixels and these specs assert on engine state, never pixels), the no-throttling Chromium launch args in `playwright.config.ts` (a backgrounded witness page otherwise stops applying server ticks), and `trace: "on-first-retry"` (continuous tracing taxed every attempt). The offline suites never touch either backend; `multiplayer.e2e.ts` and `nether-online.e2e.ts` exercise both (their shared account/registration walk lives in `e2e/onlineHelpers.ts`).

15	
16	### Fixed
17	
18	- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.
19	- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).
20	- **A bed respawn point is now honored only in its own dimension**: the spawn point stored bare block coordinates, and the same coordinates index a different voxel in each world — so dying in the Nether could false-positive on whatever happened to occupy the overworld bed's cell there. Bed spawn points now carry a dimension stamp (optional save field, additive — old saves read as overworld); respawn falls through to a safe local spot when the bed belongs to the other world.
21	- **Deflaked the simulated-latency FIFO (a real reorder, not a test artifact)**: the latency-simulation knob scheduled one `setTimeout` per delayed message, relying on the timer heap to fire equal-deadline timers in creation order — but that tie-breaking is not stable in Bun, and the monotonic delivery cursor _clamps_ every message behind a high jitter draw to the exact same deadline, making ties the common case. Result: rare genuine reordering of simulated-latency traffic (caught by the jitter-FIFO unit test going red on `main`, ~2/100 locally). Each direction now drains through a queued **delay line** — the same cursor, but one timer chain delivering in queue order, so FIFO comes from the queue rather than from timer tie-breaking; `dispose()` clears both lines, so no stray delivery timers outlive a session. Dev/testing code path only (simulated latency is never on in real play) — no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change — though the lagged multiplayer e2e steps (400±100 ms) inherit the stronger ordering guarantee.
22	- **CI: forks no longer attempt (and fail) prod deploys**: the `deploy-web` / `deploy-server` jobs now carry a `github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'` guard. The upstream repo syncs this workflow but holds none of the deploy secrets, so every push to its `main` went red on `curl -X POST ""` / an unauthenticated `flyctl deploy` — nothing ever deployed (secrets are repo-scoped), it was pure noise. Outside this repo the jobs now skip instead of fail.

Real players move immediately, which is why prod co-op never surfaced it; the flaky two-browser friend-dig e2e had been passing on server random-tick edits instead of the dig it claimed to test (its aim recipe now targets the block-underfoot center, and a new room-level regression pins a never-moved joiner's streamed `mineHeld` actually breaking the block). Engine-only: no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.

- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.

- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).

- **A bed respawn point is now honored only in its own dimension**: the spawn point stored bare block coordinates, and the same coordinates index a different voxel in each world — so dying in the Nether could false-positive on whatever happened to occupy the overworld bed's cell there. Bed spawn points now carry a dimension stamp (optional save field, additive — old saves read as overworld); respawn falls through to a safe local spot when the bed belongs to the other world.

A never-moved joiner in an online world could not mine. The server seats
every fresh joiner at exact integer coordinates — ON the cell boundary —
and the mining/aim DDA mishandled that origin two ways when a direction
component was (near-)zero: the \`dir || 1e-6\` fallback treats -0 as falsy
so its epsilon could carry the WRONG SIGN versus the already-chosen step,
and the boundary origin computed a zero first-crossing, stepping the ray
sideways into a neighbor column at t=0 on an axis it never travels.
Digging straight down from a fresh seat therefore mined the DIAGONAL
column — or nothing once that column was hollow (the host's earlier
shaft). Real players move first (fractional coordinates), which is why
prod co-op never surfaced it; the flaky friend-dig e2e had been passing
on server random-tick edits instead of the dig it claimed to test.

Fix: a zero component never steps its axis (tMax = Infinity), in BOTH
copies of the traversal (voxelRaycast and waterSurfaceRaycast). Honest
geometry is preserved: a ray genuinely tilted toward a boundary it starts
on still enters that neighbor column immediately. New degeneracy tests
pin both behaviors, and server/roomMining.test.ts pins the end-to-end
regression: a never-moved joiner streams mineHeld and the block underfoot
actually breaks. Engine-only — no save, worldgen, or protocol change." && git log --oneline -1
